Burkina Faso : Les éleveurs de la région de l’Oubri invités à adopter l’insémination artificielle
items.description: Le ministre délégué chargé des Ressources animales, le Dr Amadou Dicko, a poursuivi, ce 11 novembre 2026 dans la région du Oubri, sa tournée dans le cadre du suivi de la campagne 2026-2027 de vaccination contre les maladies animales prioritaires et de la campagne d'insémination artificielle. Il s'est rendu dans le village de Bagr Zaanga, dans la province du Zoundwéogo et dans le village de Zongnaba à Sourgoubila avec sa délégation pour rappeler aux éleveurs la nécessité d'adhérer à l'insémination artificielle des vaches. Le Burkina Faso veut replacer le secteur de l'élevage au cœur de l'économie nationale. Cela passe par la préservation du cheptel et l'accroissement des capacités de production laitière. De ce fait, le ministère chargé des Ressources animales a intensifié sur tout le territoire national la campagne de vaccination contre les maladies animales prioritaires. À travers la Direction générale des services vétérinaires, le ministère a entrepris la vaccination des petits et grands ruminants contre huit maladies, notamment la peste des petits ruminants et la pasteurellose. En plus de la campagne de vaccination, le ministère chargé des Ressources animales a lancé la campagne d'insémination artificielle des vaches. Pour cette campagne, l'objectif escompté est l'insémination de 100 000 têtes au plan national. Dans la région du Oubri, les vétérinaires ont déjà inséminé 650 vaches sur un objectif de 5 000 insémination. Cette technique aura pour objectif d'améliorer la génétique du cheptel pour une meilleure production laitière et de viande pour la consommation. Cependant, certains éleveurs sont réticents à pratiquer l'insémination artificielle. Les plus sceptiques rejettent toujours l'efficacité de cette technique pour leur cheptel. D'autres vont plus loin en indiquant que la religion interdit l'insémination artificielle sur les vaches. La pose de bolus pour l'identification des animaux©️Faso7 « Tout ce qu'on dit sur le plan religieux, nous nous sommes référés aux différents imams, aux différents prêtres, aucune prescription religieuse n'interdit l'insémination artificielle », a rassuré Ardiouma Sirima, directeur général du Centre de promotion de l'aviculture et de multiplication des animaux performants. Par contre, les éleveurs comme Issa Compaoré, ayant introduit l'insémination artificielle dans leur cheptel, se réjouissent des avantages. D'abord, elle a été subventionnée par l'État, passant du prix initial de 75 000 FCFA à 5 000 FCFA. De plus, les veaux issus de l'insémination présentent une bonne physionomie. À ce sujet, Issa Compaoré a confié qu'un particulier aurait proposé environ un million de FCFA pour acquérir son veau de 7 mois. « Alors que dans notre cheptel, nous avons des bœufs de plus de deux ans qui ne s'achètent pas à 1 million FCFA. C'est vraiment bénéfique pour nous les éleveurs », a-t-il témoigné. La campagne a aussi concerné la pose de bolus pour l'identification des animaux. C'est une identification digitalisée qui permet de lutter contre le vol de bétail et de différencier les animaux des autres troupeaux. Le système permet de suivre l'historique de la santé de l'animal ainsi que la ferme d'origine de l'animal lorsqu'il sera conduit à l’abattoir. Cheick Habib Désiré BAYILI Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : Les éleveurs de la région de l'Oubri invités à adopter l'insémination artificielle est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: ‘Importing wine doesn’t make you an economist’, Tinubu hits Obi, says Atiku has nothing to offer
items.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure President Bola Tinubu has urged Nigerians to reject opposition presidential candidates, Peter Obi and Atiku Abubakar, in the 2027 general election, saying they have nothing to offer the country. Tinubu, who spoke through Vice-President Kashim Shettima at the All Progressives Congress, APC, presidential campaign rally in Akure, Ondo State, described the opposition figures as no match for the President. Shettima challenged Obi and Atiku to present their records in public office and policy alternatives to Nigerians, rather than relying on social media campaigns. He said the opposition had failed to demonstrate what it could offer the country. Shettima takes swipe at Atiku, Obi Shettima questioned Atiku’s political standing in his home state of Adamawa, claiming that even former governors of the state were not supporting him. He also criticised Obi, alleging that his campaign relied on what he described as “obnoxious data” rather than verifiable achievements. “The ability to import cheap South African wines does not make one a guru in economics,” he said. The Vice-President described Obi’s tenure as Anambra State governor as mediocre and challenged opposition politicians to identify their major achievements in the past 25 years of democracy. Ondo leaders rally behind Tinubu Shettima said Tinubu enjoyed what he called a “universal elite consensus” in Ondo State, contrasting it with the alleged lack of support for Obi and Atiku in their respective home states. He cited former Ondo State Governor Olusegun Mimiko, former governorship candidate, Chief Olusola Oke, SAN, and member of the House of Representatives, Gboyega Adefarati, as evidence of the APC’s growing political support in the state. He also claimed that former Anambra governors Chris Ngige, Chinwoke Mbadinuju and Willie Obiano, as well as incumbent Governor Charles Soludo, were not aligned with Obi. Shettima projects 1.2 million votes With Ondo’s registered voters put at 2.1 million, Shettima said the APC was targeting at least 1.2 million votes from the 1.8 million residents said to have collected their Permanent Voter Cards, PVCs. He described the turnout at the rally as a political statement, recalling similar outings in Cross River, Nasarawa, Akwa Ibom, Rivers, Ebonyi and Jigawa states. Shettima also contrasted the opposition’s activities with what he described as Tinubu’s achievements in the last three and a half years, while commending Ondo APC leaders for putting their differences aside. Aiyedatiwa promises one million votes In his address, Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa promised to deliver one million votes for Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. Aiyedatiwa thanked the President for what he described as progressive policies and interventions, saying Ondo voted massively for Tinubu in 2023 because of his leadership record as governor of Lagos State. He said Tinubu had justified the confidence reposed in him through reforms whose benefits, according to him, had reached the grassroots. The governor also thanked the President for appointing three ministers from Ondo State, overseeing the finance, interior, and youth portfolios. He listed his administration’s achievements to include the recruitment of more than 6,000 workers, road and bridge projects, rehabilitation of health institutions and support for young entrepreneurs. “We will all go to the mountains, to the hills and everywhere to tell the people about your re-election,” he said. Yilwatda: Tinubu most prepared of 18 candidates The APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, described Tinubu as the most experienced, exposed, prepared and competent among the 18 presidential candidates expected to contest the 2027 election. Yilwatda said Tinubu had confronted the country’s economic challenges, adding that more than 31 states which, according to him, could not pay workers’ salaries when the President assumed office could now meet their obligations. Yari: Tinubu gave Ondo more than ministers’ worth The Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council and former Zamfara State Governor, Abdulaziz Yari, said Tinubu had demonstrated commitment to Ondo State through appointments and other benefits. “These five positions are equivalent to about 10 ministers in Ondo,” Yari said. He said the President had given the state considerable attention despite its not being an oil-producing state, citing infrastructure projects, the nine per cent allocation and cash transfer arrangements. Yari urged party leaders to intensify mobilisation, saying the APC was not merely seeking victory in Ondo but a substantial vote margin for Tinubu nationally. “We are not looking for Asiwaju to win in Ondo State. We are looking for Asiwaju to get millions of votes that will give the margin for the presidency,” he said. Uzodimma urges residents to collect PVCs The Chairman of the Progressive Governors Forum and Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, said Ondo had 2.4 million registered voters, but only 1.4 million had collected their PVCs, leaving nearly one million cards uncollected at INEC offices. He urged residents to collect their cards, embrace unity and put their grievances aside, describing Ondo as Tinubu’s political home. Oshiomhole: Nigeria needs statesmen, not petty traders Former Edo State Governor and Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, urged youths to support Tinubu, saying Nigeria needed statesmen rather than petty traders in politics. Oshiomhole praised Tinubu for appointing what he described as competent people into key positions, citing the Minister of Finance, and said the administration was investing in roads and railway infrastructure. He also said Tinubu had approved an additional N70,000 for federal civil servants and was committed to job creation. According to him, the President plans to undertake a major review of the power sector in his second term, with a view to doubling electricity generation and addressing transmission challenges. The senator urged youths to compare the time and resources required to establish a factory or refinery with those needed to set up a shopping mall, arguing that Obi’s business orientation was unsuitable for long-term national development. Mimiko, Oke, Bamidele pledge unity Former Ondo State Governor Olusegun Mimiko pledged to work with other political leaders to deliver votes for Tinubu and all APC candidates for the National Assembly. Mimiko commended the President for building what he described as an elite consensus on major national issues, including state police, but cautioned that the establishment of state police would not automatically end insecurity. A party leader and former governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, in Ondo State, Chief Olusola Oke, said the state’s leaders were indebted to Tinubu for projects and appointments. Oke pledged to work towards delivering the one million votes promised by Aiyedatiwa and dismissed what he described as social media propaganda against the APC. The Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, urged party leaders to rally behind Aiyedatiwa, whom he described as the state campaign coordinator, to achieve the one million-vote target. Bamidele said Tinubu had sent two messages to the party: that the January 16 election would be for the presidency and National Assembly, not the governorship, and that Aiyedatiwa remained the sole campaign coordinator but must carry all stakeholders along. He called for the inclusion of Chief Mrs Oladunni Odu, DI Kekemeke, Oke, Wale Akinterinwa and Mimiko in the campaign structure, saying unity among party leaders would make the target achievable. The Senate leader also cited Tinubu’s appointment of three ministers and two ambassadors from Ondo State, to the United Nations and Russia, respectively, saying the appointments should translate into votes for the President. Those at the rally included the Minister of Finance, Mr Taiwo Oyedele; Minister of Interior, Bunmi Tunji-Ojo; Minister of Youth Development, Ayodele Olawande; member representing Akoko North-East/North-West Federal Constituency, Ifeoluwa Ehindero; members of the State Executive Council and Ondo State House of Assembly; APC candidates and chieftains; local government chairmen; political appointees; artisans; support groups; Iyalajes and Iyalojas; and youths, among others. items.title: Kankan : Près de 200 personnes poursuivies pour exploitation minière illégale
items.description: Le procès de 194 personnes interpellées dans les préfectures de Kérouané et de Siguiri pour des faits présumés d’exploitation illégale de minerais, de dégradation de l’environnement et de défaut d’autorisation d’opérer s’est ouvert ce mercredi 11 novembre 2026 à Kankan. Parmi les prévenus figurent des ressortissants guinéens et étrangers, ainsi que des mineurs et des adultes. En raison du nombre important de personnes concernées par cette procédure, les audiences ont été délocalisées dans les locaux de la Cour d’appel de Kankan. Les débats se déroulent simultanément dans les salles d’audience A et B de cette juridiction, sous la conduite du tribunal de première instance de Kankan. Les prévenus sont poursuivis par le ministère public pour plusieurs faits présumés liés à l’exploitation minière illégale, notamment la dégradation de l’environnement et l’exercice d’activités minières sans autorisation, au regard des dispositions du Code minier et du Code de l’environnement guinéens. À l’heure où nous mettons cet article en ligne, les audiences se poursuivent simultanément dans les salles A et B de la Cour d’appel de Kankan. Cette procédure judiciaire intervient dans un contexte de renforcement de la lutte contre l’exploitation minière illégale et les atteintes à l’environnement dans les zones aurifères de la Haute-Guinée.

items.title: Hydraulique : le ministre lance « Ollele » pour répondre aux urgences d’accès à l’eau
items.description: Le ministère de l’Hydraulique et de l’Assainissement prévoit de créer un fonds dénommé « Ollele », destiné à financer des interventions urgentes pour améliorer l’accès à l’eau et à soutenir la scolarité d’élèves et d’étudiants à travers des bourses. L’annonce a été faite mercredi à Dakar par le ministre Cheikh Tidiane Dièye, à l’occasion du lancement du Village J’EAU’J, organisé en marge des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. Un fonds pour répondre aux urgences hydrauliques, mais aussi accompagner les jeunes dans leur parcours scolaire. C’est l’ambition affichée par le ministre de l’Hydraulique et de l’Assainissement, Cheikh Tidiane Dièye selon l'APS, avec la mise en place prochaine du fonds « Ollele ». « Nous voulons donner de l’eau là où c’est urgent, mais aussi accompagner les élèves et étudiants avec des bourses qui leur permettront de pouvoir financer leurs études », a-t-il expliqué. Ce dispositif tire son nom d’une fillette de 11 ans, élève dans le Ferlo, qui rêvait de devenir médecin. Selon le ministre, la jeune fille a perdu la vie dans un accident de charrette alors qu’elle était partie à la recherche d’eau. Un drame qui illustre les conséquences du manque d’accès à cette ressource dans certaines localités du pays. « Ollele sera le symbole de tout ce que je ferai dans ce ministère », a déclaré Cheikh Tidiane Dièye. Il a également indiqué avoir invité ses collaborateurs à réfléchir à un mécanisme de bourses destiné aux élèves et étudiants. Prenant part à la cérémonie, le directeur de division de la Banque mondiale pour le Sénégal, Djibrilla Issa, a rappelé que la sécurité hydrique constitue un investissement dans le capital humain, la résilience des territoires et la prospérité des générations futures. À travers le Projet de sécurité de l’eau et de l’assainissement au Sénégal (PISEA), l’institution accompagne les efforts du pays pour permettre à 600 000 personnes d’accéder à des services d’assainissement gérés en toute sécurité et renforcer la résilience de sept millions de personnes face aux inondations et aux sécheresses. Pour sa part, la présidente de l’Association des jeunes professionnels de l’eau et de l’assainissement du Sénégal (AJPEAS), Rouguiata Ba, a présenté le Village J’EAU’J comme un cadre de sensibilisation et de découverte des métiers du secteur. Ingénieure hydraulique, elle a insisté sur les nombreuses perspectives qu’offre ce domaine aux jeunes, notamment dans les sciences, les technologies et l’innovation. Organisée par le ministère de l’Hydraulique et de l’Assainissement, la Banque mondiale et l’AJPEAS, cette initiative se déroule sur trois jours sur la corniche ouest de Dakar, dans le cadre du PISEA et en marge des JOJ Dakar 2026. À travers des expositions, des échanges avec des professionnels et des activités participatives autour du spor t, du climat et de l’innovation, le Village J’EAU’J entend rapprocher les jeunes des enjeux liés à la préservation des ressources en eau et à l’assainissement. C.T.N

items.title: NIA begins Ghana Card registration for children in Upper West and Savannah on November 12
items.description: Children aged between six and 14 in the Upper West and Savannah Regions will be registered for the Ghana Card from Thursday, November 12, as the National Identification Authority (NIA) expands its nationwide exercise. The latest rollout comes after registration was completed in six other regions: Volta, Oti, Northern, Upper East and North-East. Under the arrangement, NIA officials will visit public and private schools to register eligible pupils. The exercise will run from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. each day. Children in the same age group who are not attending school can access the service at designated registration centres or schools in their communities. To establish a child’s identity, parents and guardians must present an original birth certificate, a valid Ghanaian passport or a Certificate of Acquired Citizenship. If none of these documents is available, a parent, relative or legal guardian can instead complete an Oath of Identity form. For children who have no known relatives, the NIA says two Social Welfare Officers responsible for their welfare may provide the required identity confirmation under oath. Parents are also encouraged to make available their children’s NHIS cards or membership numbers, where applicable. The Authority has stressed that adults presenting children for registration must be Ghanaian citizens, at least 18 years old, of sound mind and holders of valid Ghana Cards. It has appealed to parents, guardians, schools, traditional authorities and community leaders in the Upper West and Savannah Regions to help ensure the exercise reaches all eligible children. The NIA has further warned that anyone who provides false information or facilitates the registration of a non-Ghanaian risks prosecution, as such conduct constitutes an offence under the law. The announcement was contained in a statement issued on November 11, 2026, and signed by Williams Ampomah Emmanuel Darlas, Head of the NIA’s Corporate Affairs Directorate.

items.title: Ghana Police intercepts GH₵20m worth of fake GTP fabric
items.description: The Special Operations Team of the Inspector General of Police has intercepted counterfeit wax prints from Nigeria with imitated designs of Tex Styles Ghana Limited, producers of GTP fabrics. This follows a tip off received by the special team. The product, mainly wax prints from Nigeria was smuggled into the country without paying the required taxes to the state. The exercise forms part of an anti-counterfeit campaign by Ghanaian textile manufacturers and the Ghana Police. Speaking to journalists, Environmental Sustainability Manager at Tex Styles Ghana, Schandorf Nii Obodai, disclosed that the ceased textiles are worth about GH₵ 20 million. “When you check all the materials here including the ones in the truck load, it’s about GH₵ 20 million worth of cloth which is just going to enter the local market but for the vigilance of the team”, he said. He stated that the activities of smugglers affect the nation and tax collection and also adversely impact the operations of legal companies operating in the country. “This (smuggled goods) can be in the market for about two months even after the festive season and you can imagine the amount of taxes the state may be losing just because of these smuggled items and we as a company will be struggling to sell or produce more for the local market”. Outlining the negative impact on business operations, Mr. Obodai said the increase in smuggling of fake wax prints is the reason for the collapse of many local textile companies in Ghana. “The impact of this is deeper than you can imagine because it affects production which turns to have an impact on job for our citizens in Ghana” he said. He advised the general public to note that GTP does not operate other factories in in Africa, hence any GTP fabrics produced on the continent apart from Ghana are fake and illegal. “Often traders are being bait with the myth that this is printed by GTP in Nigeria or Côte d’Ivoire. I want to put it on record today, that GTP doesn’t have any factory in Nigeria or elsewhere in Africa producing GTP or Vlisco cloths. GTP cloths are only produced in Ghana but they copy our designs and the stamps to reproduce the imitation products”, he warned. The Intelligence Unit of the Ghana Police has taken over the investigation to apprehend all perpetrators.

items.title: Confédération AES: un conseil des ministres conjoint pour évaluer la mise en œuvre de la Feuille de route de l’An II
items.description: (Ouagadougou, le 11 novembre 2026) La capitale burkinabè abrite, les 11 et 12 novembre 2026, une session du Conseil des ministres de la Confédération des États du Sahel. Objectif : examiner la mise en œuvre de la Feuille de route de l’An II, en prélude à la prochaine session du Collège des Chefs d’État de la Confédération AES. Il s’agira, pour les ministres, de faire le point des activités de la Feuille de route de l’An II réalisées au titre des piliers Défense/Sécurité, Diplomatie et Développement, et de formuler des recommandations pour la suite du processus de consolidation de la Confédération AES. La cérémonie d’ouverture de la session du Conseil des ministres a été présidée par le ministre d’État, ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, le Camarade Général de Division Célestin SIMPORE. À ses côtés se trouvaient les Camarades Bassolma BAZIÉ, président de la Commission nationale de la Confédération AES, Karamoko Jean Marie TRAORÉ, ministre des Affaires étrangères, Dr Aboubakar NACANABO, ministre de l’Économie et des Finances, et Pingdwendé Gilbert OUÉDRAOGO, ministre de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, ainsi que les délégations ministérielles du Mali et du Niger et les experts des trois pays. Le ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, lé Général Célestin Simporé Dans son discours d’ouverture, le Camarade Célestin SIMPORE a salué les avancées enregistrées au niveau des piliers Défense/Sécurité, Diplomatie et Développement, qui ont permis une consolidation progressive de la Confédération AES. Pour lui, le pilier Défense/Sécurité constitue le socle de la survie et de la liberté des pays de la Confédération face à l’hydre terroriste et aux forces impérialistes qui cherchent à entraver leur marche. Fort heureusement, les Forces armées nationales burkinabè, maliennes et nigériennes, unies et solidaires dans le cadre de la Force conjointe de la Confédération AES, font preuve de résilience. Cette session permettra également d’harmoniser davantage leurs outils et de renforcer leur autonomie stratégique. En ce qui concerne la Diplomatie, le Chef de la délégation ministérielle du Burkina Faso a indiqué que ce pilier constitue « notre raison d’être sur la scène internationale ». Il s’est réjoui du fait que la voix de la Confédération porte désormais haut et fort les idéaux de souveraineté, de respect mutuel et de refus de toute tutelle. « En portant nos idéaux d’une seule voix, nous redéfinissons nos partenariats et les diversifions sur la base stricte de nos intérêts nationaux et confédéraux, guidés par les aspirations de nos peuples », a déclaré le Camarade ministre SIMPORE. Enfin, concernant le pilier Développement, il a donné des assurances quant à la construction d’un espace intégré et prospère, en soutien aux piliers Défense/Sécurité et Diplomatie. Pour le président de la séance, « la mise en commun de nos économies, la fluidification de nos échanges commerciaux et la valorisation de nos immenses ressources naturelles constituent les leviers indispensables pour offrir à notre jeunesse des perspectives réelles et durables, loin des mirages de l’immigration clandestine ». Cette session ministérielle se veut donc un moment d’introspection stratégique et de consolidation des acquis, une occasion idoine de passer méthodiquement en revue les trois piliers fondamentaux qui cimentent la Confédération AES, un espace en perpétuelle construction, mais dont la marche apparaît déjà irréversible. À noter qu’un sujet qui nourrit l’actualité dans l’espace confédéral a été évoqué à l’ouverture de la session ministérielle. Il s’agit du refoulement de compatriotes en provenance de la République de Guinée, une situation qui a mis en exergue la formidable solidarité et le sens de la fraternité entre les peuples de la Confédération AES. Le Camarade ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique a exprimé la profonde reconnaissance du Burkina Faso aux plus hautes autorités maliennes, dont les diligences et les orientations éclairées ont permis de faire face à ce défi. DCRP/MAE L’article Confédération AES: un conseil des ministres conjoint pour évaluer la mise en œuvre de la Feuille de route de l’An II est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: The Atlantic Announces Amanda Mull, Annalisa Quinn, and Erik Slavin as Staff Writers
items.description: As part of its continued newsroom growth, The Atlantic is announcing the return of Amanda Mull as a staff writer; the hires of Annalisa Quinn and Erik Slavin as staff writers; and the hire of Bill Tipper as a senior editor overseeing the creation and launch of The Atlantic Book Club, coming in 2027. This is a homecoming for Amanda, who was a staff writer at The Atlantic from 2018 to 2024, writing countless memorable pieces on culture, trends, fashion, and the way we live. Annalisa joins from The Boston Globe , where most recently she was the deputy editor of the Globe’s Sunday magazine, and this year wrote what’s been hailed as “The Greatest Article That Has Ever Been Written” (per The Daily Beast ) about easing mask policies at a lesbian bar. Erik is joining The Atlantic ’s Pentagon team; he was the editor in chief of Stars and Stripes and spent more than two decades at the publication, before being fired by the Defense Department this summer after he refused to bend to the department’s censorship demands. Bill is joining as a senior editor overseeing the creation and launch of The Atlantic Book Club in 2027. He was most recently an editor at The Wall Street Journal , where he produced a weekly newsletter and edited a wide variety of stories for the Journal. Below are the staff announcements from editor in chief Jeffrey Goldberg: Amanda Mull i s returning as a staff writer. Ever since that tragic day in 2024 when Amanda Mull left for her Bloombergian rumspringa , we’ve been on the hunt for someone who could replace her, someone with an acute eye, a gift for language, a deep feeling for humans and their foibles, a cockeyed sense of humor and that ineffable Mullish spark. We looked for someone who understood the weird ways of American consumerism, someone who would be willing to turn herself into a test rabbit for a set of absurd Goop products, a reporter who could explain why sweaters are bad now, why ballet flats have always been bad, why self-checkout is a failed experiment. A person who could explore obsessional behavior toward diamonds and Hermés , and who also knew which flour to use to make the best biscuits. What became known as the “Amanda Mull slot,” we learned, was impossible to fill. No matter how hard we tried, no one quite fit the bill. Until now. We have finally discovered someone who could replace Amanda Mull, and that person is … Amanda Mull. We are thrilled to let you know that Amanda has rediscovered the One True Path, and will be joining us again at The Atlantic . Annalisa Quinn is joining us as a staff writer. For the last several years, Annalisa has been writing and editing for The Boston Globe , where most recently she has served as deputy editor of the Globe ’s Sunday magazine. You are all no doubt familiar with her work, including “The Greatest Article That Has Ever Been Written” (per The Daily Beast ), a mega-viral piece about the contretemps over the masking policy at a now-immortal lesbian bar in Greenfield, Massachusetts. But her name should have been familiar to you long before that, because she’s been producing first-rate journalism and literary essays for years, at The Financial Times and as a Berlin-based freelancer for The New York Times , among other places. She also served for a decade as a literary critic for NPR. She has a capacious range, bringing empathy and intelligence to her writing about homelessness and addiction; Elvis impersonators; the researchers trying to piece together the Stasi archives; and, of course, books. Erik Slavin is coming aboard as a staff writer, joining our stellar Pentagon team. Erik is one of the most experienced and gifted defense correspondents and editors in the country. As all of you know, the Defense Department fired Erik in August after he refused to bend to the department’s censorship demands. As he wrote for us not long after, “I was fired after I said in an appearance on CBS News that my personal red line would be if the Pentagon ever instructed me not to publish a perfectly accurate story. It is telling that I am being fired for describing the most anodyne of journalistic ethics, a position that any self-respecting reporter in any free society would hold, and that the Pentagon interpreted as insubordination." I am very pleased that The Atlantic will provide a home for Erik's coverage of the Pentagon, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and the armed services. Like Stars and Stripes itself, Erik is known for his deep and knowledgeable coverage of the lives of America’s men and women in uniform. This is an important and generally under-covered subject. Erik joined Stars and Stripes in 2005, and has reported from Iraq, South Korea, and Japan, where he led coverage of the Great East Japan earthquake and nuclear disaster. From 2017 to 2025, he served as the newspaper’s bureau chief for Europe and the Middle East, overseeing coverage of Afghanistan, NATO, and Ukraine. He moved to Washington to become the editor in chief of Stars and Stripes in 2025. Earlier in his career, he reported from Capitol Hill and worked as a reporter and editor in Florida. Bill Tipper is coming onboard as a senior editor overseeing the creation and launch of The Atlantic Book Club. Building a truly original subscriber experience requires hiring a unicorn, and that’s what Bill is. After getting his Ph.D. in English, Bill left academia for the wild world of the Books Internet. At BN.com, he helped launch the Barnes & Noble Review , an independent hub for some of the best online writing about books. Years ahead of most outlets, he saw the potential for new ways to connect with people who love literature, launching an author-interview podcast and an ambitious read-along series devoted to Stephen King’s complete works. More recently, as an editor at The Wall Street Journal , he has produced a weekly newsletter and edited a wide variety of stories with exceptional rigor and foresight. Bill is widely known in the literary world for his intelligence, kindness, and energy, and we’re delighted that he has agreed to take on a project that will enrich The Atlantic for years to come. Press Contacts: Anna Bross and Paul Jackson | press@theatlantic.com

items.title: Interior Minister urges Western and Western North security councils to strengthen intelligence-sharing
items.description: The Minister for the Interior, Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak, has urged the Western and Western North Regional Security Councils (REGSECs) to strengthen intelligence-sharing and collaboration among security agencies to prevent emerging threats from escalating into major security challenges. He said timely intelligence, proactive leadership and effective coordination between security agencies and local authorities were critical to identifying and addressing security concerns before they deteriorated. Mr Muntaka made the call at a workshop on the Security and Intelligence Agencies Act, 2026 (Act 1168), organised for members of the two Regional Security Councils and Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs). He described the workshop as an important intervention to equip regional and local authorities with the knowledge needed to carry out their security responsibilities under the new law. According to the Minister, Act 1168 provides a framework for improving the coordination, management and oversight of Ghana’s security and intelligence institutions. He stressed that the effective implementation of the law would depend on stakeholders’ understanding of their respective mandates, reporting arrangements and limits of authority. Mr Muntaka encouraged the two REGSECs to use the workshop to improve their early warning systems, information-sharing, joint security planning and follow-up on security concerns within their jurisdictions. He also urged them to strengthen their respective Security Councils and establish effective communication channels with security agencies operating in their regions. The Minister cautioned against waiting for security incidents to occur before contacting the relevant authorities, emphasising the need to report emerging tensions, disputes and unusual criminal activities promptly. He expressed confidence that the workshop would provide participants with the knowledge and guidance required to implement the Security and Intelligence Agencies Act, 2026 (Act 1168), effectively.

items.title: Sardine à 30 dirhams : Mezouari interpelle sur l’accès des Marocains aux ressources halieutiques
items.description: Le prix de la sardine, devenue difficilement accessible pour une partie des ménages marocains, illustre les déséquilibres auxquels le secteur de la pêche maritime est aujourd’hui confronté. Ahmed Mehdi Mezouari, ministre délégué auprès du ministre de l’Agriculture, de la Pêche maritime et de la Souveraineté alimentaire, chargé de la Pêche maritime, appelle à revoir les priorités du secteur et à engager les ruptures nécessaires pour mieux concilier les exigences de l’exportation avec la préservation de la souveraineté alimentaire. Lors de l’examen du projet de budget sectoriel du ministère, mercredi, devant la Commission des secteurs productifs à la Chambre des représentants, le responsable gouvernemental a mis en question les choix qui ont jusqu’ici privilégié les débouchés extérieurs, parfois au détriment de l’accès des consommateurs marocains aux ressources halieutiques nationales. « Pourquoi la sardine se vend-elle à 30 dirhams ? », s’est-il interrogé, estimant que cette question constituerait un enjeu majeur pour le gouvernement à l’avenir. Longtemps considérée comme un produit de consommation courante, régulièrement présent sur les tables marocaines et accessible à toutes les catégories sociales, la sardine est désormais hors de portée d’une partie de la population. Pour le ministre délégué, cette évolution révèle la nécessité de repenser les mécanismes de gestion et de valorisation des ressources maritimes. L'enjeu, a-t-il expliqué, consiste à rétablir un lien entre la richesse halieutique nationale et le consommateur marocain. Les performances du secteur ne peuvent être appréciées uniquement à travers les volumes exportés et les recettes générées. Elles doivent également être évaluées à l’aune de leur contribution à l’approvisionnement du marché national et à l’amélioration de l’accès des citoyens aux produits de la mer. Une nouvelle approche devrait ainsi replacer les dimensions sociale et alimentaire au centre des politiques publiques. Cette réorientation suppose, selon Mezouari, de dépasser les cadres stratégiques actuels. Le gouvernement s’oriente vers une nouvelle génération de stratégies, qui devra s’accompagner d’engagements et de pratiques renouvelés. Le ministre a, dans cette perspective, appelé les différents acteurs et intervenants du secteur à participer à l’élaboration d’une décision collective nationale définissant les grandes orientations de la pêche maritime pour les prochaines années. La particularité de cette activité tient notamment à la nature même de la ressource exploitée. Contrairement à d’autres secteurs économiques, les ressources halieutiques ne peuvent être directement maîtrisées. Leur gestion nécessite donc des arbitrages publics précis et une responsabilité collective, a souligné le ministre délégué. Leur préservation ne saurait relever de la seule génération actuelle : elle engage également les générations futures. Cette exigence impose, selon lui, des politiques anticipatives capables de garantir la durabilité des stocks et leur renouvellement. Au-delà des enjeux économiques et environnementaux, le ministre a également placé la situation des professionnels de la mer parmi les priorités de son département. Il a insisté sur la nécessité de préserver la dignité des marins, particulièrement exposés aux conséquences des périodes de repos biologique. Ces interruptions temporaires de l’activité, indispensables à la préservation des ressources, se traduisent en effet par une perte de revenus pour les professionnels concernés. Le ministère a engagé des discussions afin de mettre en place des dispositifs d’accompagnement et d’indemnisation durant ces périodes. Les négociations menées avec la Caisse nationale de sécurité sociale (CNSS) connaissent, selon Mezouari, une évolution positive. L’objectif est de parvenir à des mécanismes de protection sociale adaptés aux particularités de l’activité des marins et à leurs conditions professionnelles. Le Maroc dispose pourtant d'une position de premier plan dans le secteur halieutique, aussi bien à l’échelle africaine qu’internationale. Le ministre a rappelé le leadership du Royaume sur le continent et son rang parmi les principaux exportateurs mondiaux de sardines. Un positionnement qui, à ses yeux, doit désormais s’accompagner d’une réflexion sur la valeur ajoutée produite par le secteur et sur la répartition des bénéfices tirés de l’exploitation des ressources maritimes. Cette réflexion conduit également à réexaminer les résultats de la stratégie « Halieutis », lancée en 2009. Mezouari a reconnu les avancées enregistrées par ce programme, notamment en matière d’exportations et de recettes fiscales. Il a toutefois estimé que l’attention accordée à ces indicateurs avait laissé au second plan certaines problématiques sociales. Le bilan de cette stratégie appelle ainsi, selon lui, à réévaluer plusieurs choix et à corriger les déséquilibres accumulés. Pour engager cette réorientation, le ministre délégué plaide pour l’organisation d’un dialogue national réunissant l’ensemble des parties concernées, y compris les citoyens. Les discussions devraient porter sur les modalités de gestion des ressources halieutiques, la répartition des retombées économiques et les responsabilités respectives des différents intervenants. Enfin, Mezouari souhaite faire de cette concertation une véritable échéance politique nationale, au cours de laquelle les acteurs concernés pourraient s’accorder sur le devenir du secteur et les réformes à entreprendre. « Celui qui doit donner quelque chose doit le donner, et celui qui doit recevoir quelque chose doit le recevoir », a-t-il déclaré, résumant ainsi son appel à un compromis collectif sur les engagements et les changements nécessaires. The post Sardine à 30 dirhams : Mezouari interpelle sur l’accès des Marocains aux ressources halieutiques appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: PTI lawyers meet Imran at Adiala jail following IHC orders
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Lawyers representing the PTI met party founder and former prime minister Imran Khan on Wednesday, a day after the Islamabad High Court (IHC) issued orders allowing the meeting. On Tuesday, the IHC, while hearing appeals filed by Imran and his wife, Bushra Bibi, against their convictions in the £190 million reference , directed authorities to facilitate meetings between Imran and his legal team. PTI lawyer Awais Younus Chaudhry, speaking to Dawn, said Barrister Salman Safdar and Advocate Latif Khosa held a meeting with Imran. “As per orders of the court, the meeting was held to discuss under-trial cases,” Chaudhry said. The lawyers remained at Adiala for four hours and left without speaking to the media or PTI lawyers, Chaudhry said. “As their cell phones are switched off, it’s too early to say whether they were allowed to meet Imran together or separately and for how long,” he said. Later, the party posted a video of Khosa speaking to reporters about the meeting. In the video, a smiling Khosa replied in the affirmative when asked whether Bushra Bibi was also present for the meeting. He said that discussions focused on Imran’s health and the cases against him. Khosa said that details regarding Imran’s health and what he himself saw would be released later. Asked about Imran’s health, the lawyer said that Imran had a “blood pressure problem”. He said that the ex-premier’s blood pressure fluctuated to a “terrifying extent”, but added that he was “completely active and his will was very strong”. Confirming that discussions had also covered a possible 28th constitutional amendment, Khosa said that he would not go into more detail at this time. Asked why the meeting took so long, Khosa laughed and said, “Ask those who allowed the meeting.” He said that the IHC had ordered that the meeting should not be less than an hour long. The meeting took place hours after the ex-premier was again taken to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) for his eye ailment. According to the hospital , Imran was brought to Pims last night for a medical check-up and follow-up eye treatment. It added that his vital parameters were “normal”, he was clinically “stable” and his general physical examination was “normal”. Imran has been in prison since August 5, 2023 , while his wife was arrested on January 17, 2025, in a separate case in which the couple were sentenced. The IHC has allowed Imran twice-a-week meetings — on Tuesdays and Thursdays — with his family, lawyers and other associates. Despite multiple court directives , Imran’s meetings with his family and party leaders have been largely restricted . On Nov 2, Safdar met Imran after a gap of seven months for less than an hour. When he had met Imran in April, months after the ex-premier’s eye condition had surfaced , the Supreme Court had designated Safdar as amicus curiae. However, on Nov 2, he met Imran as his lawyer. PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram, speaking to Dawn after the Nov 2 meeting, said that no political issues were discussed as Safdar spoke about the cases and asked about future strategy. When asked about Imran’s health, Akram replied that although health issues were discussed, the PTI would only speak about the legal cases.

items.title: Apo-Karshi road to become Abuja tourist attraction – Wike
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said the Apo-Karshi road, a project awarded in 2010 but abandoned for years, will be developed into a tourist attraction in Abuja. Wike spoke on Wednesday during an inspection of the completed road in the nation’s capital. He attributed the completion of the project to President Bola Tinubu’s intervention, saying the President ordered the termination of the original contract after the contractor failed to deliver despite receiving full payment. “This road was awarded in 2010 to an indigenous contractor. We did all we could to persuade the contractor to ensure that the job was fully implemented, even though we had fully paid. But the contractor was not forthcoming,” he said. According to the minister, the matter was brought to Tinubu’s attention, following which the President directed that the contract be terminated and re-awarded to a more competent company. Wike said the decision was informed by the strategic importance of the road to residents and the overall development of the FCT. He added that the administration was not deterred by criticism over the cost of the new contract. “When this contract was awarded, some people were asking how we could award it at that amount. But we were not deterred. All we were concerned about was the happiness and comfort of the people,” he said. Wike described the road as one of the most publicised projects undertaken by the Satellite Towns Development Authority (STDA), noting that the difficult terrain made its completion a remarkable engineering achievement. He said reactions on social media showed that many Nigerians were surprised that a project of such scale and engineering complexity could be delivered in the country. The minister also acknowledged journalists for drawing public attention to the project, saying their reports had helped Nigerians appreciate the scale of work carried out on the road. He urged Nigerians to assess the Tinubu administration’s performance holistically rather than judging it based on isolated issues. “Look at what is going on in Abuja today, the level of infrastructure and how it has turned out to be a tourist centre. I am happy that people are happy and that Nigerians have seen the infrastructure development being carried out by the Tinubu administration,” he said. On the commissioning of the road, Wike said the FCT Administration was working around the President’s schedule, as several other projects were also being lined up for inauguration. He expressed hope that Tinubu would inaugurate the Apo-Karshi road before the end of November, adding that efforts would be made to secure a place for the project in the President’s schedule. On plans for public facilities around the road, the minister said the administration would develop appropriate amenities in collaboration with relevant departments. items.title: Two dead after clash between residents, illegal miners and NAIMOS personnel at Manso Keniago
items.description: Two people have died following a confrontation involving residents, suspected illegal miners and personnel of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) at Manso Keniago in the Ashanti Region. Two deaths have been confirmed, although the circumstances surrounding the fatalities remain unclear. Further details, including the identities of the deceased, the extent of injuries and the response of the security personnel, are yet to be established. items.title: Éducation et formation : Le Président nigérien reçoit la délégation ministérielle de l’AES conduite par Jacques Sosthène Dingara
items.description: En marge de la Conférence des ministres chargés de l’Éducation et de la Formation de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES), le Président de la République du Niger, le Général d’Armée Abdourahamane TIANI, a reçu en audience, hier mardi 10 novembre 2026, au Palais de la Présidence à Niamey, une délégation ministérielle de l’AES conduite par le Ministre burkinabè chargé de l’Enseignement de base, Jacques Sosthène DINGARA. Composée également d’Amadou SY SAVANE, Ministre malien de l’Éducation nationale, et d’Oumou SALL SECK, Ministre malienne de l’Entrepreneuriat, de l’Emploi et de la Formation professionnelle, la délégation a transmis au Chef de l’État les salutations fraternelles du Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ et du Général d’Armée Assimi GOÏTA. Elle lui a également rendu compte des travaux de la Conférence ministérielle. Le Président nigérien, Chef de l'État, le Général d'Armée Abdourahamane TIANI, s’est réjoui de la tenue de ces travaux, qu’il a présentés comme une traduction de la volonté commune des trois pays de bâtir une éducation de qualité, adaptée à leurs réalités et au service de la jeunesse et de la souveraineté de la Confédération. Les Ministres ont, pour leur part, indiqué avoir reçu mandat de mettre en place ce cadre de concertation afin de construire des systèmes éducatifs ancrés dans les réalités socioculturelles des peuples de l’AES. L’ambition est notamment de promouvoir les cultures nationales, le patriotisme et le civisme, tout en formant une jeunesse capable de contribuer au développement de la Confédération. Plusieurs membres du Gouvernement nigérien ont pris part à l’audience, notamment le Ministre Directeur de Cabinet du Président de la République, Dr Soumana Boubacar, le ministre de l’Enseignement technique, Dr Farmo Moumouni, et la Ministre de l’Éducation nationale, Dre Elisabeth Shérif. DCRP MEBAPLN

items.title: Police avert communal crisis as youths clash over colleague’s death in Kaduna
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The Kaduna State Police Command has averted a possible communal crisis following a clash between rival youth groups from Kwaru and Unguwar Yero communities in Kaduna North Local Government Area of the state. The incident, which reportedly left some people injured, occurred on Wednesday morning following tension over the death of a youth who sustained injuries during an earlier confrontation between young people from the two communities. The deceased, reportedly from Unguwar Yero, was said to have died from injuries sustained during the disagreement about a week ago, triggering anger among his friends, who allegedly attempted to avenge his death on Wednesday. The development caused panic among residents, with some schoolchildren reportedly fleeing their schools as rival groups engaged in stone-throwing and other acts of violence. A resident of Kwaru, who identified himself as Sule, said the incident occurred around 9am when he heard noise and came out to see youths throwing stones at one another. “Some youths from Kwaru and Unguwar Yero had a disagreement about a week ago, during which a young man was injured and later died. “On Wednesday, after the children had gone to school, we started hearing noise. When I came out, I saw people gathering, while some were throwing stones at one another between the youths from Unguwar Yero and some residents of Kwaru who had gone to the cemetery,” he said. Sule said the incident heightened tension in the area, recalling that the two communities had experienced similar disagreements in the past before relative peace was restored. He confirmed that operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS), police and Mobile Police (MOPOL), among other security personnel, were deployed to the area to prevent further escalation and restore normalcy. Another resident, Mohammed, expressed concern over recurring disagreements among young people from the two communities. He said many of the youths were friends who often gathered together, adding that it was unfortunate that disagreements between them were sometimes given ethnic or religious interpretations. “They are youths who are friends, but whenever there is a disagreement among them, some people try to turn it into an ethnic or religious issue. That is not right,” he said. A teacher in the area, Bashir, also confirmed that three youths sustained injuries during the earlier confrontation, adding that one of them later died. He, however, said normal activities had started returning to the communities following the deployment of security personnel. There were also indications that the tension threatened to spread to neighbouring communities before security operatives intervened. The Kaduna State Police Command spokesman, DSP Mansir Hassan, confirmed the incident, saying the situation had been brought under control following the deployment of security personnel. “The situation is under control following a massive deployment of security personnel to the communities,” he said. The police intervention prevented the disagreement from degenerating into a wider security crisis, even as residents called for sustained security presence and peaceful engagement among youths and community stakeholders to forestall further violence. It was not confirmed as of the time of filing this report whether a curfew had been imposed on the affected communities. The post Police avert communal crisis as youths clash over colleague’s death in Kaduna appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NULGE slams withholding of Osun LG funds, urges immediate resolution‎
items.description: ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — THE Nigeria Union of Local Government Employees (NULGE) has condemned the continued withholding of statutory allocations due to local governments in Osun State and called for urgent intervention from the Federal Government and other relevant stakeholders. ‎ ‎The union said the development had deepened the leadership and funding crisis in the state’s local government system, prompting workers to stage a warning strike from Sunday, November 8, to Wednesday, November 11, 2026. ‎ ‎In a statement jointly signed by its President-General, Comrade Aliyu Haruna, and General Secretary, Comrade Gambo Isah, NULGE stressed that local government workers should not suffer the consequences of political disputes, leadership tussles or administrative faentitlement ‎ ‎According to the union, the Supreme Court’s affirmation of local government financial autonomy must go beyond legal recognition and produce real financial independence, improved services, and timely payment of workers’ dues. ‎ ‎It noted that local government autonomy would be of little value without access to funds, cautioning that councils could not function effectively when their finances were withheld and workers’ legitimate entitlements were denied ‎ ‎NULGE consequently “called for the immediate resolution of all outstanding issues surrounding the release and accessibility of funds due to local governments in Osun State.” ‎ ‎It also demanded “an urgent and lasting resolution of the leadership crisis in the state’s local government system in accordance with constitutional and legal provisions.” ‎ ‎The union further urged authorities to protect workers against salary delays, denial of entitlements and victimisation arising from the crisis. ‎ ‎It called on the Federal Government, Osun State Government and other relevant stakeholders to intervene and engage constructively to restore normalcy and industrial harmony in the state. ‎ ‎Expressing solidarity with the leadership and workforce of NULGE in Osun State, the national leadership assured the workers that the union would not abandon its responsibility to defend their rights, welfare and dignity. ‎ ‎While urging the affected workers to remain peaceful and disciplined, NULGE “called on all parties to demonstrate political maturity and genuine commitment to resolving the crisis without further delay.” ‎ ‎The union warned that “the continued withholding of local government funds is not merely a labour issue but also a threat to grassroots democracy, effective service delivery and the economic survival of thousands of Nigerian families.” ‎ ‎It declared that the time for political blame games was over, insisting that decisive action was needed to end the crisis and protect the interests of local government workers across the country. items.title: 2027: Atiku can’t unite Adamawa, let alone Nigeria — Shettima
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Vice-President Kashim Shettima has questioned whether African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar can unite Nigeria, claiming the former Vice-President lacks political consensus in his home state of Adamawa. Shettima made the claim while campaigning for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election at the APC presidential campaign rally in Akure, the Ondo State capital, on Wednesday, setting up a contrast between what he described as weak opposition support in Adamawa and Anambra and the broad backing for the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ondo. The Vice president argued that the political alignments in the three states showed the difference between the opposition’s position and the support Tinubu had gathered for his re-election bid while noting that former vice president Atiku had not secured the backing of any of Adamawa’s five governors since the return to democracy in 1999. “Our political opponents can conduct political rallies on Facebook and on Instagram, but for somebody who cannot build a consensus at the home front, Atiku Abubakar is from Adamawa state. He has been unable to build a lead consensus, even in his own Adamawa State,” Shettima said. “Of all the five governors that have ever ruled Adamawa State in the current dispensation—from Mr. Boni Haruna to Vice Admiral Murtala Hamman-Yero Nyako to Barrister Bala James Ngilari to Senator Muhammadu Umaru Jibrilla (Bindow) to Rt. Hon. Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri—none of these governors and former governors are in alignment with Atiku Abubakar. He also listed prominent politicians in the state whom he said were not aligned with the ADC candidate. “All the political mavericks in Adamawa State, from the former SGF Boss Gidahyelda Mustapha to Engineer Babachir David Lawal, to Senator Aishatu Dahiru Ahmed (Binani), and all the major political actors in Adamawa State, are not in alignment with Atiku.” Shettima also cited the political divisions in Adamawa as evidence, saying they raised questions about Atiku’s ability to unite the country. “And right now, he has three gubernatorial candidates in Adamawa. So someone who cannot unite his own state, I wonder how he is going to unite and drive the nation as a whole,” he said. The Vice president then contrasted his account of the opposition’s support in Adamawa with the turnout for Tinubu in Ondo, describing it as a demonstration of backing for the President’s re-election. “Here in Ondo, Ondo, the game is over. This is a shutdown. Nothing less is expected from Ondo, and we remain eternally grateful to the people of Ondo for the massive turnout and support accorded to Mr. President,” he affirmed. Shettima also criticised National Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate Peter Obi over his attempt to welcome the victorious Flamingos, Nigeria’s U-17 women’s football team, at Abuja airport on Monday. “And you know, it is cheap to vie for the presidency of Nigeria, especially for those like my big friend Peter Obi, who think clout chasing like he went out of protocol to welcome our young victorious Flamingos, the female footballers and teams. You just must have grassroots and stakeholder support,” Shettima said. He also questioned Obi’s political support in Anambra, asking whether former governors Chris Ngige and Willie Obiano, or incumbent Governor Charles Soludo, were aligned with him. “When the president says he ran away from erosion, believe me, he did. But then, how many of the first governors of Anambra are with him? Is Chris Ngije with him? The answer is no. Is Willie Obiano with him? The answer is no. Is my friend Charles Chukuma Soludo with him? The answer is no,” he said. Returning to Ondo, Shettima described Tinubu’s support in the state as a broad political consensus, citing former Governor Olusegun Mimiko, lawyer Olushola Oke and members of the late Governor Adebayo Adefarati’s family. ““And for the people of Ondo, as we are talking, there is a universal elite consensus marking the president here in Ondo. Former Governor Olusegun Mimiko is firmly on board. The last opponent, very popular Olushola Oke SAN, is here in alignment with the president’s ambition,” “Even the son of late Governor of Ondo State, Bayo Adefarati, who represents Akoko Southeast and Akoko Southwest. The son former Governor Adebayo Adefarati is in alignment with the APC, which indicates that the whole family is within the same APC family. There has to any bargain, there has to be any consensus behind any progressive movement,” he said.” The post 2027: Atiku can’t unite Adamawa, let alone Nigeria — Shettima appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Shettima accuses Obi of ‘clout chasing’ over Flamingos, says he went ‘out of protocol’
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Vice-President Kashim Shettima has accused Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate Peter Obi of “clout chasing” after the former Anambra governor said he was prevented from welcoming Nigeria’s victorious U-17 women’s team, the Flamingos, at Abuja airport on Monday. Shettima referred to the incident while campaigning for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Akure, the Ondo State capital, on Wednesday. Obi said he had asked to greet the players when he saw them at the airport after their return from Morocco, where they won the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. However, the National Sports Commission(NSC) disputed aspects of his account, saying the request was not arranged in advance and that people claiming to be his protocol officers approached the team while it was being escorted to buses. While criticizing Obi’s political approach, Shettima said seeking the presidency required grassroots and stakeholder support, and described Obi’s airport appearance as an attempt to attract attention. “And you know, it is cheap to vie for the presidency of Nigeria, especially for those like my big friend Peter Obi, who think clout chasing like he went out of protocol to welcome our young victorious Flamingos, the female footballers and teams. You just must have grassroots and stakeholder support,” he said. The Vice-President also challenged Obi’s record as Anambra governor, citing former governors Chris Ngige, Willie Obiano and incumbent Charles Soludo, whom he said were not supporting him. “When the president says he ran away from erosion, believe me, he did. But then, how many of the first governors of Anambra are with him? Is Chris Ngije with him? The answer is no. Is Willie Obiano with him? The answer is no. Is my friend Charles Chukuma Soludo with him? The answer is no,” Shettima said. Shettima then questioned Obi’s economic credentials, arguing that importing South African wine did not make someone an economic expert. He described Obi’s performance as governor as “at best mediocre” and challenged him to identify his major accomplishments during 25 years of democratic governance. “Your Excellencies, distinguished ladies and gentlemen, the ability to import cheap South African wines doesn’t make one a guru in economics. Peter Obi, in spite of all his pretensions about the knowledge of the economy, his performance as governor of Anambra state was at best mediocre, and Peter Obi called Lagos home. So that goes to show that he is benefiting from the quality of leadership provided by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in Lagos. I challenge him to come out and tell us specifically their major accomplishments in the past 25 years of democratic governance in this country,” he said. Turning to Ondo State, Shettima said Tinubu had the backing of political figures across the state, including former governor Olusegun Mimiko, the late governor Adebayo Adefarati’s family and lawyer Olushola Oke, whom he described as a popular former opponent to incumbent governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa. “And for the people of Ondo, as we are talking, there is a universal elite consensus marking the president here in Ondo. Former Governor Olusegun Mimiko, his firmly on board. The last opponent, very popular Olushola Oke SAN, is here in alignment with the president’s ambition. Even the son of late Governor of Ondo State, Adebayo Adefarati, who represents Akoko Southeast/Southwest is in alignment with the APC, which indicates that the whole family is within the same APC family. There has to any bargain, there has to be any consensus behind any progressive movement,” Shettima added. items.title: Insecurity: Become security managers, minister tells unity college principals
items.description: …Demands stronger surveillance, intelligence networks, emergency plans By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Government has urged principals of Federal Unity Colleges to assume greater responsibility for school security, warning that rising insecurity, particularly banditry, insurgency and student abductions, poses a growing threat to Nigeria’s education system. The Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Sa’idu Ahmad, gave the charge on Wednesday in Abuja, urging principals to move beyond their traditional roles as academic administrators and embrace proactive security management to prevent schools from becoming soft targets for criminal elements. Ahmad spoke at the 2026 Annual General Meeting of Principals of Federal Unity Colleges, held under the theme, “Nigerian Schools in the Midst of Insecurity: Building Safe, Resilient and Sustainable Learning Environments.” She said increasing incidents of banditry, insurgency, student abductions and communal conflicts had exposed educational institutions to unprecedented security risks, requiring urgent and coordinated action by school administrators. According to her, the consequences of insecurity extend beyond physical attacks on schools, as they also cause psychological trauma among students, disrupt academic activities, increase absenteeism, worsen the out-of-school children crisis and discourage teachers from accepting postings to vulnerable communities. The minister warned that failure to secure schools could undermine years of investment in education and jeopardise the future of millions of Nigerian children. She particularly highlighted the vulnerability of Federal Unity Colleges, noting that their boarding-school structure, which accommodates children from different parts of the country away from their families, requires specialised security arrangements and closer administrative supervision. Ahmad described the colleges as critical instruments of national integration, bringing together children from diverse ethnic, religious, geographical and socioeconomic backgrounds. “Today’s Federal Unity Colleges principals cannot just be instructional leaders; they must also be active, forward-thinking security managers,” she said. Outlining the Federal Government’s approach to tackling insecurity in schools under President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, Ahmad identified four strategic areas requiring urgent attention. These, she said, included strengthening physical security infrastructure through improved perimeter fencing, controlled entry and exit points and electronic surveillance systems; establishing community-based intelligence networks involving traditional rulers and other stakeholders; expanding psychosocial support and trauma-informed counselling for students; and deploying digital technology to sustain teaching and learning during emergencies. She urged principals to institutionalise regular security assessments, conduct emergency drills, establish effective communication channels with security agencies and develop school-specific emergency response plans. The minister also stressed the importance of transparent, inclusive and supportive school environments, arguing that building trust among students, teachers and administrators was essential to identifying potential threats and responding effectively. She assured the principals that the Federal Ministry of Education remained committed to improving their welfare and mobilising resources to strengthen security infrastructure across Federal Unity Colleges. Earlier, the Chairman of Principals of Federal Unity Colleges, Alhaji Shehu Dahiru, called for stronger government intervention to address worsening insecurity, teacher shortages, inadequate funding and infrastructure deficits affecting the administration of the institutions. Dahiru said security challenges across the country had continued to undermine school enrolment, attendance, academic calendars, staff morale and parents’ confidence in the safety of their children. He maintained that protecting schools should not be regarded as the exclusive responsibility of security personnel, insisting that principals, teachers, students, parents, host communities, traditional institutions, security agencies and government must work together. He called for improved perimeter protection, access-control systems, surveillance equipment, emergency communication facilities, early-warning mechanisms and regular security drills across the colleges. The chairman also warned against allowing insecurity to permanently derail the educational ambitions of Nigerian children, urging vulnerable schools to establish learning-continuity arrangements. Such arrangements, he said, should incorporate digital and offline learning resources, alternative teaching methods, psychosocial support and structured catch-up programmes to ensure students do not lose valuable learning time during emergencies. Beyond security concerns, Dahiru appealed to the Federal Government to accelerate teacher recruitment and professional development, particularly in science, technology, mathematics, English, technical and vocational education. He said shortages of qualified teachers in critical subject areas were placing additional pressure on the colleges and threatening the quality of education delivered to students. He also called for sustained funding to upgrade and maintain laboratories, workshops, ICT facilities, hostels, water and sanitation facilities, electricity supply and other essential infrastructure. The chairman identified staff welfare, shortages of non-teaching personnel, feeding costs, operational expenses and inadequate health services as other challenges requiring urgent government attention. Despite the challenges, he commended the Federal Government’s ongoing education reforms, particularly the Technical and Vocational Education and Training programme, teacher professional development initiatives, digital learning, curriculum improvement, anti-bullying measures and student welfare interventions. He pledged the commitment of principals to translating government policies into measurable improvements in teaching, learning and institutional administration. Dahiru further called for a coordinated national mechanism to guarantee learning continuity and strengthen school safety, involving the Federal Ministry of Education, National Senior Secondary Education Commission, Federal Quality Assurance Service, security agencies, state education authorities, traditional institutions, Parent-Teacher Associations, alumni associations and development partners. He said security agencies should provide professional guidance and coordinate responses to emerging threats, while education authorities should ensure effective policy implementation and provide the necessary emotional and institutional support. Parents and host communities, he added, should assist in identifying and reporting potential security threats, while alumni associations and private-sector organisations should contribute resources, expertise and innovative solutions. He stressed that the survival of Nigeria’s education system amid mounting security challenges would depend on the collective commitment of stakeholders to protecting learners, supporting teachers and building institutions capable of withstanding emergencies. items.title: Kenya: le dernier malade d’Ebola libéré de l’hôpital
items.description: Le Kenya franchit une étape importante dans sa lutte contre Ebola. Le dernier patient atteint du virus a quitté l’hôpital, ce mercredi 11 novembre 2026, a annoncé le ministre de la Santé, Aden Duale. Cette évolution marque le début du compte à rebours de 42 jours nécessaire avant que le pays puisse être officiellement déclaré exempt de la maladie. Les autorités sanitaires kényanes affichent leur soulagement après la sortie d’hôpital du dernier malade d’Ebola encore sous traitement. Selon le ministre de la Santé, Aden Duale, cette étape ouvre désormais une période de surveillance de 42 jours, au terme de laquelle le Kenya pourra être déclaré exempt du virus, en l’absence de nouveaux cas. Dès la détection du premier malade, les autorités avaient identifié 135 personnes ayant été en contact avec lui, afin de limiter les risques de propagation de la maladie. À cette occasion, Aden Duale a défendu la gestion de l’épidémie par son gouvernement, mettant en avant la transparence et le respect des règles sanitaires internationales. «Nous avons opté pour la transparence dès les premières heures. Nous avons signalé les cas très tôt, publié nos chiffres, partagé nos données et maintenu nos frontières ouvertes», a-t-il souligné. Le ministre a toutefois déploré les restrictions générales de voyage et de visas imposées au Kenya par certaines juridictions en réaction à l’épidémie. Il a appelé les autorités concernées à lever ces mesures sans délai, estimant que le pays ne compte désormais plus aucun patient sous traitement. Pour rappel, le Kenya avait enregistré neuf cas d’Ebola au mois d’octobre, après l’arrivée sur son territoire d’un premier malade en provenance de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), via l’Ouganda. Le virus s’était ensuite propagé à quatre membres de sa famille ainsi qu’à quatre professionnels de santé. Le bilan de cette flambée épidémique fait état de deux décès, ceux du patient initial et de sa mère. Les sept autres personnes contaminées ont, quant à elles, complètement recouvré la santé. À l’échelle régionale, l’épidémie continue de susciter des préoccupations, avec plus de 11 000 cas recensés depuis son apparition en mai. La sortie du dernier patient kényan constitue ainsi un signal encourageant, même si le pays devra encore franchir les 42 jours de surveillance sanitaire avant de pouvoir tourner officiellement la page de cette crise. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Kenya: le dernier malade d’Ebola libéré de l’hôpital est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Reps to probe rising human trafficking, trafficking networks
items.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has resolved to investigate the rising incidence of human trafficking in Nigeria, mandating its Committees on Human Rights, Interior and Police Affairs to probe the activities of trafficking syndicates and assess the effectiveness of existing measures to combat the crime. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion sponsored by Rep. Dominic Okafor, titled, “Need to Investigate the Alarming Increase in Human Trafficking in Nigeria”, at Wednesday’s plenary. The lawmakers expressed concern over the growing threat posed by human trafficking, particularly to women, children and other vulnerable groups. The House noted that human trafficking remained a grave violation of human rights and dignity, involving the recruitment, transportation, transfer, harbouring or receipt of persons through force, coercion, deception, abuse of vulnerability or other prohibited means for the purpose of exploitation. It observed that victims were increasingly subjected to commercial sexual exploitation, forced labour, domestic servitude, forced begging, organ harvesting and other forms of degrading abuse. The lawmakers attributed the growing vulnerability of Nigerians to trafficking to poverty, unemployment, insecurity, displacement, irregular migration and the activities of organised criminal networks. They further noted that many victims were lured through false promises of employment, education, marriage and opportunities abroad, only to end up in exploitative conditions characterised by physical abuse, psychological trauma and, in some cases, death. The House also expressed concern that trafficking networks operated across state and international borders, exploiting porous borders, inadequate public awareness, weak coordination among relevant agencies and difficulties in identifying and prosecuting offenders. While acknowledging the efforts of the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Immigration Service and other relevant institutions, the lawmakers stressed the need to strengthen their operational capacity, funding, intelligence-sharing and victim-support mechanisms. The House recalled the provisions of the Trafficking in Persons (Prohibition) Enforcement and Administration Act, 2015, and other relevant legislation aimed at preventing trafficking, prosecuting offenders and protecting victims. Consequently, the lawmakers urged the Federal Government to intensify nationwide efforts to combat human trafficking through effective enforcement of existing laws, intelligence-led investigations and prosecution of traffickers and their collaborators. They also called for improved victim identification, rescue, rehabilitation, psychosocial support, legal assistance and reintegration programmes, particularly for women, children and other vulnerable persons. The House further urged the government to address the underlying factors exposing Nigerians to trafficking, including poverty, unemployment, limited access to education and the exploitation of displaced persons. NAPTIP and other security and law enforcement agencies were also urged to strengthen surveillance, intelligence-sharing and coordinated operations against trafficking networks, particularly those operating across state and international borders. The lawmakers called on the Federal Ministry of Education, relevant state ministries, local government authorities, civil society organisations and community leaders to intensify public enlightenment campaigns on traffickers’ tactics and the dangers of deceptive recruitment and irregular migration. The House subsequently mandated its Committees on Human Rights, Interior and Police Affairs to investigate the scale and patterns of human trafficking in Nigeria, examine the activities of trafficking syndicates and assess the adequacy of existing enforcement measures. The committees are also expected to identify challenges confronting agencies responsible for combating the crime and report their findings to the House within four weeks for further legislative action.
