items.title: NEEMBA Burkina : Emir SANOH prend les commandes de la filiale
items.description: NEEMBA Burkina a officiellement présenté son nouveau directeur pays, Emir SANOH, le 23 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou. Le dirigeant burkinabè entend poursuivre les acquis de la filiale et renforcer son accompagnement auprès des acteurs des mines, de la construction, de l’énergie et de l’industrie. La cérémonie s’est déroulée autour d’un cocktail, en présence de collaborateurs, de partenaires, d’amis et de membres des familles. À cette occasion, Éric Jean-Noël ZOURÉ a passé le relais à son successeur, dans une ambiance conviviale. Ingénieur de formation, Emir SANOH exerce dans les secteurs des infrastructures industrielles, de l’énergie, de l’aéronautique, entre autres. Il entre ensuite dans le groupe NEEMBA en 2023, ou il occupe plusieurs fonctions en Côte d’Ivoire, au Togo et au Bénin, avant sa nomination à la tête de la filiale burkinabè. Une responsabilité à la tête d’une filiale historique Cette nomination, pour le nouveau directeur pays, constitue à la fois une fierté et une responsabilité. Il entend préserver les acquis de cette entreprise, présente au Burkina Faso depuis plus de cinquante (50) ans. « Je représente le groupe chez moi, dans mon pays. […] Il faudrait que je la laisse dans un état aussi bon que celui dans lequel je l’ai récupérée », a-t-il déclaré. Emir SANOH entend ainsi s’inscrire dans la continuité du travail engagé par son prédécesseur. Il salue des équipes « engagées, dynamiques et compétentes » et privilégie un management fondé sur la proximité avec les collaborateurs et les partenaires. Son ambition est de rester à l’écoute de leurs préoccupations, tout en tenant compte des réalités du contexte national. Le contenu local au cœur de sa vision Au-delà de la continuité managériale, le nouveau directeur pays place l’accompagnement des clients au cœur de ses priorités. Il entend notamment soutenir le développement des activités minières et des projets d’infrastructures au Burkina Faso. Dans un contexte où les autorités burkinabè encouragent une exploitation accrue des ressources nationales, Emir SANOH met l’accent sur le contenu local. Il souligne que NEEMBA Burkina compte plus de 500 collaborateurs, dont 99 % sont burkinabè, et dispose d’infrastructures implantées à proximité de ses clients. La filiale dispose notamment de sites à Gampèla et Dassasgho à Ouagadougou, à Bobo-Dioulasso et bientôt à Banfora. Ces installations permettent d’assurer la maintenance des équipements utilisés par les opérateurs miniers et les entreprises de construction. Elles offrent également des capacités de reconstruction complète de certains engins miniers, dont les camions. « Nos forces, ce sur quoi nous nous appuyons, c’est vraiment une expertise locale » , a souligné Emir SANOH. Cette approche permettrait, selon lui, au groupe d’accompagner les ambitions du Burkina Faso en matière de valorisation de ses ressources et de développement de ses infrastructures. Un groupe présent dans 11 pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest Concessionnaire officiel de Caterpillar depuis 1932, NEEMBA est un groupe industriel panafricain présent dans onze (11) pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest. Il intervient principalement dans les secteurs des mines, de la construction, de l’énergie et des équipements industriels. En 2023, le groupe a adopté l’identité NEEMBA, inspirée du mont Nimba, symbole de son ambition d’excellence. Cette nouvelle identité s’inscrit dans une dynamique de développement portée par une gouvernance africaine. Éléonore Savadogo Faso7 L’article NEEMBA Burkina : Emir SANOH prend les commandes de la filiale est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Culture sésame : 24 916 ha emblavés, 18 573 tonnes produits et 14 000 tonnes exportées
items.description: Des experts et chercheurs sénégalais se sont réunis, du 10 et 11 novembre 2026, au Ceeras-Isra de Thiès, pour valider les résultats d'une vaste enquête menée auprès de 1000 producteurs, afin de structurer et de développer la filière sésame à travers le pays. Cette étude sur la chaîne de valeur du sésame au Sénégal a été menée par le Centre international d’amélioration du maïs et du blé (Cimmyt) et l'Institut Sénégalais de Recherches Agricoles (Isra), dans le cadre de l'initiative Vision for Adapted Crops and Soils (Vacs). Dans un contexte de changements climatiques, les cultures alternatives, comme le sésame, gagnent en popularité grâce leur forte résistance aux aléas climatiques et à la sécheresse. Ce projet vise principalement à favoriser la transformation locale des produits et à réduire les exportations de matières brutes pour que la valeur ajoutée profite directement à l'économie nationale. L’étude a révélé que pour y parvenir, il est essentiel de soutenir l'industrialisation du secteur, d'améliorer les équipements de récolte et d'accompagner les transformatrices dans l'accès aux marchés internationaux. Le sésame, un oléagineux tolérant à la sécheresse, riche en nutriments et dont la demande internationale est croissante, fait partie des cultures traditionnelles bien adaptées aux conditions locales, mais peu étudiées. A travers l'initiative Vacs, co-organisée par le Cimmyt et la Fao, a lancé une étude s’est déroulée en deux phases, d’abord en mars 2026 sur l’analyse fonctionnelle de la chaine de valeur et à partir d'avril à juin 2026 une enquête auprès de 1 000 ménages producteurs de sésame dans 116 villages répartis dans 9 régions du Sénégal. L’étude a relevé que le sésame est bien adapté aux conditions arides du Sahel ouest-africain et suscite un intérêt croissant au Sénégal en tant que culture de rente alternative. En 2024-2025, le Sénégal a produit environ 18 573 tonnes sur 24 916 hectares, dont une part importante a été exportée (14 000 t). Cependant, la productivité reste faible, à environ 745 kg/ha. Par ailleurs, il est noté que les données sur la chaîne de valeur du sésame au Sénégal « restent extrêmement limitées ». D’où la faiblesse des connaissances sur « la manière dont les petits producteurs produisent, transforment et commercialisent le sésame, sur les acteurs et les flux matériels et économiques le long de la chaîne de valeur, sur les besoins en main-d’œuvre et les opportunités d’emploi, ou sur les dynamiques de genre, d'âge et sociales ». L’étude a fait ressortir que ce « manque de données limite la capacité des décideurs et des praticiens à concevoir des interventions qui créent des emplois ruraux inclusifs et des moyens de subsistance durables pour les acteurs de la chaîne de valeur du sésame, y compris les femmes et les jeunes ». Les résultats ont révélé que la chaine de valeur du sésame au Sénégal est « largement informelle et centrée sur l'exportation de graines brutes ». Les petits et moyens producteurs produisent environ 18 573 tonnes par an, dont la majeure partie est vendue sous forme de graines brutes, à environ 300 F.Cfa/kg, directement aux grands commerçants ou à des petits et moyens commerçants, qui revendent aux grands commerçants à environ 300-375 F.Cfa/kg. Il est à noter que « les producteurs dépendent principalement de sources informelles de semences, dont la plupart issues des récolte, estimées à 1579 tonnes par an, ou des semences recyclées sur les marchés informels (environ 450-1 000 F.Cfa/kg). Les circuits formels sont limités et peu de producteurs cultivent des variétés améliorées. Peu de producteurs utilisent des intrants achetés, comme les engrais et les pesticides, qui proviennent principalement de fournisseurs privés d'intrants. En ce qui concerne la transformation locale et la valeur ajoutée sont limitées, le constat est qu’une petite part de la production (environ 371 tonnes par an) est transformée, en huile alimentaire, en collations et en huile cosmétique, vendues dans les supermarchés et sur les marchés publics ou informels. L’enquête quantitative a mis en exergue une productivité faible de sésame, cultivé avec peu d'intrants pour un rendement moyen était d'environ 272 kg/ha et le rendement médian d'environ 200 kg/ha. Considérée comme une culture de rente, les ménages producteurs vendent environ 88 % de leur récolte de sésame, leur principale source de revenus monétaires mesurée. Ce qui explique que la valeur ajoutée soit presque inexistante avec environ 2 % des ménages qui conservent une partie de leur récolte pour la transformer. Mbaye Sarr DIAKHATE, correspondant

items.title: 2027: Why Atiku won’t win Adamawa – Shettima
items.description: ….Sets 1.2m votes target for Ondo APC By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: President Bola Tinubu has questioned the capacity of former vice president and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC, Atiku Abubakar to win the 2027 presidential election, saying the former customs chief cannot command consensus even in his home state of Adamawa. The president also queried Peter Obi’s credentials, saying the ability to import cheap South African wines doesn’t make one a guru in economics. Tinubu spoke on Wednesday at the All Progressives Congress APC Presidential Campaign Rally in Ondo State, where he was represented by his vice, Kashim Shettima. The president also set a target of 1.2 million votes for the party in the state. “Our political opponents can conduct political rallies on Facebook and Instagram, but for somebody who cannot gain a consensus at the home front, Atiku Abubakar is from Adamawa State. He has been unable to achieve consensus even in his own Adamawa State. “Of all the five governors that have ever ruled Adamawa in the current dispensation, from Mr Boni Haruna to Murtala Nyako, to James Bala Ngilari, to Senator Mohammed Bindow Jibrilla, to Right Honourable Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri, none of these governors and former governors are in alignment with Atiku Abubakar. And right now, he has three gubernatorial candidates in Adamawa State.. How he is going to unite and drive the nation?”, he asked. Shettima also took on Mr Peter Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC, asking how many former Anambra State governors were with him. “Is Chris Ngige here with him? The answer is no. Is Willie Obiano with him? The answer is no. Is my friend Charles Chukwuma Soludo with him? The answer is no.” He said Obi’s economic credentials were overstated. “The ability to import cheap South African wines doesn’t make one a guru in economics.” Turning to Ondo, Shettima said the state had rallied behind the President. “There is a universal elite consensus backing the President here in Ondo,” he said, naming former Governor Olusegun Mimiko among those aligned with the APC. On the target, he said: “You have registered voters of 2.116 million, we hope that on the 16th of January next year, we hope that the minimum votes we expect from Ondo is 1.2 million votes out of the 1.8 million who have collected their PVCs.” Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa had earlier promised the President “a minimum of one million votes”. He said: “Ondo State stands by you. You have given us more than enough reason to elect you.” The Director General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, said that figure was too modest. “This one million votes said by Governor, as the DG of the Asiwaju Presidential Campaign Committee, is still small,” he said. He told the gathering: “We are not looking for Asiwaju to win by a margin. We are looking for Asiwaju to get millions of votes that will give the margin for the presidency.” The National Chairman of the APC, Nentawe Yilwatda, said 18 candidates had been presented by 18 political parties ahead of the 16 January presidential election. “Among those 18 candidates, who has the wisdom of experience, wisdom of exposure, wisdom of preparation and wisdom of purpose?” he asked. Yilwatda said Tinubu had met that test. “He has confronted the economic challenges of Nigeria, and he has stabilised the economy. He came when more than 31 states could not pay salaries. Today, all of them can pay salaries.” The Governor of Imo State, Senator Hope Uzodimma, said the uncollected Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) were a threat to the target. “Your PVCs are still lying at the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) offices, very close to one million yet to be collected. The question is, without your PVC, how will you support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu? You must come out en masse, drop all grievances, be enthusiastic, and vote massively for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu”, he urged. The post 2027: Why Atiku won’t win Adamawa – Shettima appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Électrification rurale : L’Agence Faso Vêenem outille les collectivités territoriales de cinq régions à Koudougou
items.description: Réunis du 11 au 13 novembre 2026 à Koudougou, les acteurs des collectivités territoriales de cinq régions renforcent leurs capacités en matière de recrutement des concessionnaires d’électrification rurale. Cette initiative de l’Agence Faso Vêenem vise à garantir une gestion efficace et durable du service public de l’électricité. L’accès durable à l’électricité en milieu rural ne dépend pas uniquement de la réalisation des infrastructures, mais également de leur bonne gestion. C’est dans cette perspective que le ministère de l’Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, à travers l’Agence Faso Vêenem, organise, du 11 au 13 novembre 2026 à Koudougou, un atelier de renforcement des capacités des collectivités territoriales sur le recrutement des concessionnaires d’électrification rurale. À l’ouverture des travaux, le directeur général de l’Agence Faso Vêenem, Dr Edmond Lankouandé, a insisté sur l’importance d’une sélection rigoureuse des opérateurs chargés de l’exploitation des infrastructures électriques. « Au-delà de la réalisation des infrastructures électriques, il importe de garantir leur exploitation durable à travers la sélection d’opérateurs disposant des capacités techniques, financières et organisationnelles nécessaires » , a-t-il souligné. Il a également précisé les résultats attendus de cette session : « Nous attendons de ces travaux des résultats concrets, notamment la mise à disposition des Conseils régionaux concernés des dossiers techniques nécessaires au recrutement des concessionnaires et l’élaboration de feuilles de route opérationnelles » . Dr Edmond Lankouandé, DG de l’Agence Faso Vêenem Représentant le président de la délégation spéciale régionale du Nando, Pousbila Rosalie Ouédraogo a salué le choix de Koudougou pour abriter cette rencontre. Pour elle, « l’accès à l’énergie constitue un facteur déterminant du développement économique et social de notre territoire » . Elle a ainsi invité les participants à formuler des recommandations pertinentes et à prendre des engagements clairs pour la réussite du processus. Du côté des participants, les attentes portent essentiellement sur la maîtrise des procédures. Soumaïla Sanon, secrétaire général du Conseil régional du Djôrô, souhaite notamment « maîtriser le cadre juridique institutionnel en matière d’électrification rurale » , ainsi que le contenu des dossiers types d’appel d’offres et les responsabilités des différents acteurs. Même attente chez Nathalie Lallogo, responsable de la commande publique du Conseil régional du Yaadga : «Nous attendons qu’au sortir de cette session de formation, nous ayons tous les outils nécessaires pour conduire à bien l’électrification rurale qui sera désormais confiée aux collectivités » , a-t-elle affirmé. Elle rappelle également que « l’électricité, c’est la base de tout » . Réunissant des représentants des régions du Nando, du Oubri, du Yaadga, du Nazinon et du Djôrô, cet atelier ambitionne de promouvoir des procédures de recrutement transparentes et conformes à la réglementation. À terme, il s’agit de faire des collectivités territoriales des acteurs pleinement outillés pour assurer une exploitation efficace des infrastructures et améliorer durablement l’accès des populations rurales à l’électricité. Faso7 L’article Électrification rurale : L'Agence Faso Vêenem outille les collectivités territoriales de cinq régions à Koudougou est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Par sa capacité d’autorévolution, le Parti communiste chinois consolide un socle essentiel pour l’unité et le progrès des pays du Sud global (Par Par S.E.M. LI Zhigang)
items.description: Récemment, le 5e plénum du XXe Comité central du Parti communiste chinois (PCC) s’est tenu avec succès à Beijing. Cette session a adopté une décision sur les questions d’intérêt majeur relatives à la poursuite inlassable de l’autogouvernance intégrale du Parti avec rigueur, qui établit un cadre systématique pour renforcer cette discipline dans la nouvelle ère et lors de la nouvelle marche, offrant ainsi une garantie politique solide pour soutenir l’édification d’un pays puissant et le grand renouveau de la nation par la modernisation chinoise. Ce plénum constitue une opportunité précieuse pour décrypter les clés du succès de la gouvernance du PCC. Depuis sa fondation il y a 105 ans, le PCC a toujours conservé l’autogouvernance rigoureuse du Parti comme caractéristique distinctive. À l’époque, dans une grotte de Yan’an, le Président Mao Zedong a apporté la première réponse à la question de savoir comment briser les cycles historiques de l’ordre et du désordre, de la grandeur et de la décadence : « permettre au peuple de surveiller le gouvernement ». Depuis le XVIIIe Congrès du Parti, le Comité central du PCC rassemblé autour du Camarade Xi Jinping a trouvé dans la pratique la deuxième réponse pour consolider son statut de Parti au pouvoir à long terme : « pratiquer l’autorévolution ». Persévérant à « pointer le couteau vers son propre sein », le PCC demeure à l’avant-garde du progrès et de la préservation de sa pureté. L’autogouvernance intégrale et rigoureuse du Parti a créé une nouvelle atmosphère pour « la gouvernance du PCC ». En Chine aujourd’hui, plus de 92 % des personnes interrogées affirment éprouver un sentiment d’accomplissement, de bonheur et de sécurité, tandis que le taux de satisfaction vis-à-vis du gouvernement dépasse 90 %. La sécurité, l’innovation, le développement vert, l’ouverture et le partage sont désormais les traits marquants de « la gouvernance à la chinoise ». L’une des idées directrices de la Décision consiste à mettre en œuvre intégralement la pensée de Xi Jinping sur l’édification du Parti. Cette pensée trouve son origine dans la théorie scientifique du marxisme, s’enracine dans la belle culture traditionnelle chinoise et se nourrit de la grande pratique du PCC en matière d’autogouvernance, d’autodéveloppement et d’autorenforcement de plus de cent ans, forme un paradigme théorique efficace en matière de gouvernance et de discipline du Parti. Portant une vision mondiale, elle guide le PCC à renforcer sans cesse ses capacités en matière de direction politique, d’orientation idéologique, d’organisation des masses et de mobilisation de la société, tout en subissant des trempes révolutionnaires, et apporte également des outils aux autres pays du Sud ainsi qu’aux partis politiques du monde entier pour renforcer leur aptitude à gouverner et à préserver la vitalité et la santé de leur structure. ——Le renforcement des capacités de direction politique repose sur la constitution d’une force dirigeante solide et la mise en place d’une structure organisationnelle rigoureuse, garantissant une communication fluide entre les différents échelons ainsi qu’une exécution efficace des décisions. Il s’agit là du préalable et de la garantie de la stabilité politique et du développement national, ainsi que de la clé pour préserver l’autonomie du développement dans un contexte international complexe et changeant. —— Le renforcement de la capacité d’orientation idéologique se traduit par l’indépendance et la confiance en soi, ainsi que par l’utilisation des théories scientifiques pour armer l’ensemble du Parti, éduquer le peuple et guider l’action. Chaque parti politique, fort de ses spécificités et de son contexte propre, doit intégrer sa gouvernance au processus de modernisation nationale, tout en tenant compte de ses réalités intérieures et en explorant de manière autonome sa propre voie de gouvernance. ——Le renforcement de la capacité d’organisation des masses s’incarne dans la ligne fondamentale : « Tout pour les masses, tout s’appuyer sur les masses ; venir des masses, aller aux masses ». L’adhésion ou le rejet du peuple est le facteur décisif qui détermine le destin d’un parti et d’un régime. Tant que le Parti préservera ses liens viscéraux avec les masses populaires, sa cause connaîtra un succès inéluctable. ——La capacité de mobilisation de la société se renforce en offrant aux populations des perspectives prometteuses, en les orientant par des stratégies scientifiques, en les motivant par les acquis du développement et en les influençant par une conduite exemplaire. En conjuguant la direction du Parti et la souveraineté populaire, on fédère divers groupes et ressources pour constituer une force puissante au service de la modernisation du pays. Le PCC demeure attaché à sa mission : œuvrer au bonheur du peuple chinois, au renouveau de la nation chinoise, ainsi qu’au progrès de l’humanité et à l’harmonie à l’échelle mondiale. À ce nouveau point de départ historique, la Chine, guidée par l’esprit du 5e plénum du XXe Comité central du PCC, persiste dans sa volonté d’autorévolution et de rigueur dans l’autogouvernance du Parti. Elle poursuit résolument la voie de la modernisation à la chinoise, favorise un développement de haute qualité et une ouverture accrue, tout en s’engageant fermement en faveur de la paix mondiale et du développement partagé. La Chine et le Sénégal sont des compagnons de route et de bons frères sur la voie du développement et du redressement. L’année des JOJ de Dakar 2026 coïncide avec celle des « échanges humains et culturels sino-africains ». Ces deux événements se font écho et insufflent une dynamique nouvelle aux échanges entre civilisations ainsi qu’à la coopération mutuellement bénéfique. Ils constituent un fruit précieux de l’amitié entre la Chine, le Sénégal et, plus largement, l’Afrique, marquant un nouveau point de départ pour l’édification d’une communauté de destin sino-sénégalaise. À l’avenir, la Chine réaffirme son soutien indéfectible au Sénégal dans le choix d’une voie de développement adaptée à ses réalités nationales. Ensemble, nous ambitionnons de renforcer le partage d’expériences en matière de gouvernance, d’élever le partenariat de coopération stratégique global sino-sénégalais à un niveau supérieur et d’ouvrir un nouveau chapitre dans la modernisation conjointe des pays du Sud global. Par S.E.M. LI Zhigang, Ambassadeur de la République populaire de Chine au Sénégal

items.title: Withheld Osun LG fund: National public sector union body backs Osun strike
items.description: *Warns FG of total shutdown By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Umbrella body for public sector union in the country, the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council, JNPSNC, Trade Union Side, has thrown its weight behind the three-day warning strike declared by the Osun State Council of the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, over the continued withholding of statutory allocations meant for local government areas in the state by the Federal Government. The national leadership of the council described the industrial action as justified, warning that the prolonged withholding of local government funds, which it said had lasted for about 21 months, had inflicted severe economic hardship on local government workers and their dependants. It called on the Federal Government to immediately release the outstanding allocations to prevent an escalation of the industrial dispute. The national body also cautioned that the continued withholding of the funds could undermine grassroots administration and deepen the economic difficulties confronting workers across Osun State, stressing that urgent intervention was necessary to avert a total shutdown. In a statement by the National Secretary of JNPSNC, Gbenga Olowoyo, on behalf of the national leadership, the council said: “The National leadership of Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council JNPSNC (Trade Union Side), under the Chairmanship of Comrade Benjamin Anto Uyanto mni, has thrown its weight behind the current three days strike called by the Osun State Council of the Nigeria Labour Congress NLC over the continued withheld of the Local government fund by the Federal Government. “The JNPSNC reviewed all the circumstances surrounding the reason for the solidarity strike called by the Osun State Council of NLC, which was premised on the urgent need to release the withheld statutory allocation due to local government areas in the state since February 2025, that is now about 21 months of withholding the fund (from February 2025 to November 2026) and considered it as very justifiable. “The National leadership of JNPSNC considered the continued withheld of the Osun State local government fund by the Federal Government is not only excessive use of political power but also reckless without conscience, on account that the far reaching negative implications on the economic fortunes of the local government administration on one hand and the economic subjugation on the local government workers and their dependants on the hand is better imagined than experienced. “Consequent upon the cry of the entire workers in Osun State, it is very desirable for the Federal Government and all concerned to release the fund without further delay in order to allow Osun State local government workers and their dependants to have economic breath. “The National leadership of JNPSNC regretted that under democratic administration the Federal Government and its agencies responsible for the withheld allocations could descend so low to the extent of using Federal power to undermine the effective administration of local government in Osun State, which is the closest to the people in the grassroots and the essence of democracy itself in the real sense of it. “Flowing from the above, the Federal Government should be sensitive and responsive enough to listen to the cry of Osun State workers and their dependants and release the withheld allocations funds to Osun State local government which is about 21 months now (i.e. from February 2025 to November 2026) without further delay. “The National leadership of JNPSNC commended the State Chairman NLC, Dr Christopher Arapasopo, as well as TUC, JPSNC and the entire leadership of organised Labour in the State for providing responsible and well coordinated leadership direction during this crucial period in the lives of Osun State Local government workers. “From the look of things and the economic death sentence the local government workers in Osun State Council are passing through, the three-day warning strike may dovetail to total strike or protest by Osun State workers against the Federal Government if the non-release of withheld Osun State local government funds persists. “A stitch in time will save nine.” The post Withheld Osun LG fund: National public sector union body backs Osun strike appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Scottish DJ, 32, confirmed as victim of Krakow shooting
items.description: A 32-year-old Scottish man has been confirmed as one of the victims of a mass shooting in Poland that left six people dead. The man, who is understood to be James Thomas Campbell from Prestwick in South Ayrshire, died when a lone gunman opened fire in central Krakow on Saturday. Campbell worked as a DJ in Ayrshire. Police Scotland confirmed it was providing specialist support to the victim’s family, but formal identification is yet to be carried out. The 24-year-old attacker, named as Michal Oksinski by local media, died in hospital on Monday, having also fatally shot four Polish citizens and an Austrian woman with a further 15 people, including two police officers, injured. Det Ch Insp David McAlinden, senior investigating officer from Police Scotland’s Counter Terrorism Policing unit, said the force was “aware of the tragic death of a Scottish man in Krakow”. He added: “Working in conjunction with COPFS (the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service), Police Scotland is supporting the UK counter-terrorism policing network and the Polish authorities. “The immediate shared priority is to ensure that identification is properly established for the family, so that repatriation can take place as quickly as possible. “The family has asked for their privacy to be respected. Our thoughts are with them and everyone impacted by this incident.” The attack began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow’s Main Market Square, a popular tourist spot. Police said the gunman drove into the square before beginning to fire at random people from his car. Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the man, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning. In addition to the six people killed in central Krakow, police later found the bodies of the gunman’s parents and sister at his address on Saturday. Earlier this week two friends from Aberdeen described how they ran for their lives as the shooting started. Ciaran McMenemy, 26, and Charlie Hutchison, 27, said they had just sat down for a drink when the gunfire began. They quickly fled and took shelter.

items.title: Kennedys sue to block Trump’s arch, arguing it would cast shadow on JFK’s grave
items.description: The family of former US President John F Kennedy has sued to block construction of a triumphal arch that President Donald Trump plans to build in the nation’s capital. Nine members of the political dynasty argue the 250ft (76m) structure would block the view of Kennedy’s grave, as well as the graves of thousands of veterans buried at Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia. Last week, a US judge temporarily halted the project on the heels of a vote allowing construction to proceed. The White House said it was “unfortunate” to see that some members of the Kennedy family had joined litigation against an arch “intended to honor our heroes who rest in Arlington Cemetery”. “The judiciary should not be abused to politicize a structure designed to unite our nation,” White House spokesman Davis R Ingle said in a statement to the BBC. “We will continue making the case for this beautiful and fitting monument and are confident we will be fully vindicated as this litigation proceeds,” he added. Last week the project won approval from the National Capital Planning Commission. But US District Judge Tanya Chutkan then ruled there should be a 14-day pause before any work can start on the arch as litigation plays out. The Kennedy family filed its complaint under a joint lawsuit brought by the state of Virginia and Washington DC seeking to block construction, arguing that the arch will damage “historically significant sightlines” if erected at the gateway of the cemetery. The plaintiffs include seven children of Robert and Ethel Kennedy, as well as their grandson – former Democrat congressman Joe Kennedy – and Ted Kennedy’s son Edward Kennedy Jr. It does not include Trump cabinet official Robert F Kennedy Jr, who leads the Department of Health and Human Services. Their motion moves to intervene in two other lawsuits filed by conservationists and veterans seeking to halt the construction. They say the arch would be a “permanent denigration” of the gravesites and that the Kennedy offspring “would never again be able to appreciate both sites as they always have before, and as the Kennedy family always intended”. The Kennedy family argues the structure “will permanently cast shadows over and damage historically significant sightlines to the existing gravesites and memorials established in the Kennedy family’s honor” at the cemetery. The structure would also “fundamentally alter the experience of visiting the gravesites”, including the memorials of hundreds of thousands of US veterans, the Kennedys said. The complaint said that the National Park Service and Interior Department authorised construction on 5 November 2026 without the necessary congressional approval. The so-called Arc de Trump is one of the president’s efforts to remake the capital city and is meant to commemorate the country’s 250th anniversary. Last year, he also added his name to the Kennedy Center, a major Washington DC cultural institution named in honour of JFK. Trump’s name remained on the facade for six months until the addition was ruled illegal and removed.

items.title: ‘How many Ghanaians sleep at 6pm?’ Agalga defends evening Budget presentation
items.description: Majority Leader James Agalga has dismissed concerns by the Minority over the 6:00 p.m. presentation of the 2027 Budget, insisting that Ghanaians will be wide awake to follow the Finance Minister’s address. Speaking in Parliament on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, Mr Agalga said the government did not intend to present the budget at a time when the public would be asleep. “We are not intent on presenting a budget statement when the people of this country are asleep. That is not what we are intending to do,” he said. His comments followed criticism by Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin, who questioned why Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson had chosen to present the budget in the evening. Mr Agalga challenged the Minority’s suggestion that the timing would leave Ghanaians too tired to follow the presentation. “But how many Ghanaians go to sleep at 6:00 p.m? With the greatest of respect, how many Ghanaians? Honourable Osei Kyei-Mensah-Bonsu, do you sleep at 6:00 p.m? No. Ghanaians will be wide awake to listen to the presentation of the new economy,” he said. He added that the public would be interested in the government’s plans to create jobs, particularly for young people. “They are eager to know how government would create jobs for the teeming youth of our country. So nobody would sleep. They’ll be wide awake to listen to the good news that we have for the good people of this country,” he said. Mr Agalga also explained that the evening schedule was influenced by an important state function planned for Thursday, November 12. He said the government would launch new currency notes on the same day, an event at which the Finance Minister was expected to be present. “Tomorrow there is an important state function. We are launching new currency notes. And we all know that the Finance Minister plays a critical role so far as the finances of our country are concerned. And therefore would be in attendance when the notes are being launched,” he said. He added that the Speaker of Parliament, Alban Bagbin, and the Minority Leader had also been invited to the launch. Dr Cassiel Ato Forson is scheduled to present the 2027 Budget to Parliament on Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. Speaker Alban Bagbin announced on Tuesday that he had granted the Finance Minister’s request for an evening presentation, citing “good reasons”.

items.title: Zamfara: Jaji wins APC rerun primary by 26,646 votes
items.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau A member representing Kaura-Namoda/Birnin Magaji Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Hon. Aminu Sani Jaji, has won the All Progressives Congress (APC) fresh primary election for the constituency with a landslide victory. Jaji emerged winner of the rerun primary conducted on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, polling 26,646 votes to defeat his closest challenger, Hassan Umar Dangaladima, who scored 713 votes. The third aspirant, Musa Zubairu, polled no votes. The Chairman of the APC Electoral Committee for the Kaura-Namoda/Birnin Magaji fresh primary, Hon. Kabiru Idris, announced the results at the constituency’s collation centre in Kaura-Namoda. Giving a breakdown of the exercise, Idris said the constituency had 42,266 registered party members, out of whom 27,389 were accredited to vote, while 27,359 votes were cast. In the results announced, Jaji scored 14,264 votes in Kaura-Namoda Local Government Area, against Dangaladima’s 465 votes, while Zubairu scored zero. In Birnin Magaji Local Government Area, Jaji polled 12,382 votes, while Dangaladima secured 248 votes. Zubairu again scored zero. Declaring the result, Idris said Jaji had satisfied the requirements of the law, the APC constitution and the party’s guidelines, and was therefore returned as the winner of the fresh primary. The rerun followed a suit filed by Dangaladima at the Federal High Court, Abuja, which nullified Jaji’s earlier nomination and ordered the party to conduct a fresh primary within two weeks. The APC national leadership subsequently fixed November 11, 2026, for the rerun, in compliance with the court’s order. items.title: APC chieftain to DSS: Scrutinise Dino Melaye’s statements
items.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi An All Progressives Congress (APC) chieftain and loyalist of President Bola Tinubu, Khamis Musa Darazo, has urged the Department of State Services (DSS) and other security agencies to scrutinise recent statements attributed to former Kogi West Senator, Dino Melaye, concerning the 2027 general elections. Darazo, who made the call while speaking with journalists in Bauchi on Thursday, said the move was necessary to safeguard national security and prevent political utterances capable of heightening tension or creating unnecessary apprehension among Nigerians. He, however, cautioned that his call should not be interpreted as an attempt to intimidate opposition politicians or suppress democratic freedoms, stressing that democracy accommodates criticism, disagreement and healthy political competition. According to him, political leaders must recognise the responsibility that comes with public statements, particularly as the country approaches another election cycle. “This is not about persecution, intimidation or silencing the opposition. It is about responsibility. If a statement made by a prominent political actor has generated legitimate security concerns, the authorities have every right to seek clarification and establish the facts,” he said. Darazo maintained that security agencies must apply the law fairly, irrespective of political affiliation, warning against the use of national security as a partisan instrument. He also urged Melaye and other political leaders to exercise restraint in their public statements, saying Nigeria could not afford another atmosphere of political tension, fear and confrontation ahead of the 2027 elections. “Political disagreement is normal in a democracy. What is unacceptable is allowing political competition to gradually become a source of tension among citizens. We should sell our ideas, present our records and persuade Nigerians rather than create unnecessary anxiety,” he added. The APC chieftain challenged opposition politicians to focus their campaigns on policies, programmes, leadership capacity and verifiable records rather than provocative statements capable of distracting attention from issues affecting Nigerians. He said supporters of President Tinubu were prepared for the 2027 political contest and would continue to defend the administration based on its policies, achievements and Renewed Hope Agenda. “We are not afraid of opposition. We welcome competition. But competition must be democratic, peaceful and issue-based. President Tinubu will be judged by Nigerians based on his record, just as every opposition politician will be judged by the people based on what they offer,” Darazo said. He called on the DSS and other relevant security institutions to remain professional, impartial and guided by the law in handling politically sensitive matters. He further urged political actors across party lines to place the country’s peace, unity and democratic stability above personal and partisan interests. “The 2027 election should be a contest for the confidence of Nigerians, not a contest that puts the peace of Nigeria at risk. We can disagree politically without becoming enemies of the Nigerian state,” he said. The post APC chieftain to DSS: Scrutinise Dino Melaye’s statements appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mahama leads 81st Remembrance Day commemoration in Accra
items.description: President John Mahama has led the commemoration of the 81st Annual Remembrance Day service at the Christiansborg War Cemetery in Accra, paying tribute to fallen soldiers of the First and Second World Wars and living veterans. The ceremony, held on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, featured flag-raising and wreath-laying ceremonies in honour of those who lost their lives in the two World Wars. President Mahama, who is also Commander-in-Chief of the Ghana Armed Forces (GAF), laid a wreath on behalf of the government and people of Ghana. He was followed by the British High Commissioner to Ghana, Christian Rogg, who laid a wreath on behalf of the Commonwealth and Allied countries, while Sierra Leone’s High Commissioner to Ghana, Mohammed Hassan, laid one on behalf of the diplomatic community. The Chief of the Defence Staff, Lieutenant General William Agyapong, laid a wreath on behalf of the Ghana Armed Forces, while the Chairman of the Governing Board of the Veterans Administration Ghana, Rear Admiral Peter Kofi Faidoo (Rtd), laid one on behalf of veterans. Nii Shippi Akwetey Atsu IV, representing the Osu Alata Mantse, Nii Kwabena Bonne V, also laid a wreath on behalf of traditional authorities. President Mahama and other participants observed a minute’s silence in honour of the departed. The President also signed the Book of Remembrance to reaffirm the nation’s gratitude and preserve the memory of the sacrifices made by Ghana’s fallen heroes. In a sermon, the Director of Naval Religious Affairs, Very Reverend David Benedict Quayson, commended veterans for their courage and bravery in the line of duty. He also urged personnel of the Ghana Armed Forces to remain committed to maintaining peace in Ghana and across the world. The ceremony was attended by the Minister for Defence, Kenneth Gilbert Adjei; members of the Council of State; the Military High Command; heads of sister security services; members of the Diplomatic Corps; and representatives of the Veterans Administration Ghana.

items.title: Hundreds of Italian schools hit by threats in suspected bomb hoax
items.description: Some 300 schools across Italy have received bomb threats, according to Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara, who described the incidents as probably a “cyber-attack, not a genuine risk”. Valditara told Italian TV that there was a clear strategy behind the rash of threats in Italy and elsewhere in Europe which had targeted flights, supermarkets and even hospitals. The emails were sent to schools in Rome, Naples, Vicenza, Florence, Pisa, Trieste and many other Italian cities, and a number of buildings were evacuated as a precaution. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has called a meeting of top ministers and intelligence chiefs. Meloni said the government was monitoring closely the “numerous reports of bomb threats at educational institutions” although checks so far had not indicated any evidence of “concrete danger”. “These reports appear rather linked to a strategy intended to cause alarm and concern,” she said on Facebook. Italian airports along with airlines elsewhere in Europe were hit by a series of bomb hoaxes last week that prompted a series of scares, evacuations and widespread disruption. Although a number of threats were claimed by an extremist misogynistic group, it later denied any link to the false warnings. Italian reports said 280 school head teachers had received threats in recent days. Although many schools were initially evacuated on Wednesday, the alarm was quickly lifted, according to reports from a number of regions, and pupils were allowed to return to class. In a statement, the head of the central Umbria region Stefania Proietti said “checks conducted so far in Umbrian schools have proved negative, and law enforcement is working rapidly and carefully to verify each report”. In a separate incident, more than 300 schools in Northern Ireland were sent emails which police said they were treating as a hoax. Messages sent to number of schools in Scotland were also being treated by police as a hoax. It is unclear whether any of the incidents are connected.

items.title: Philip Nai & Friends partners La Traditional Council for 7th Christmas outreach
items.description: Philip Nai & Friends has partnered with the La Traditional Council to host the seventh edition of its annual Christmas Charity Outreach for underprivileged children on Thursday, 24 December 2026. The event will take place at the La Traditional Council premises from 9:00 am as part of the initiative’s commitment to spreading love, hope and joy among children during the Christmas season. The partnership has received the endorsement of the La Traditional Council, which has expressed excitement about working with the initiative. “We are excited about this partnership with Philip Nai & Friends to bring smiles, joy and hope to underprivileged children in La this Christmas. We believe every child deserves to feel loved, valued and celebrated, regardless of their circumstances. This initiative reflects the spirit of community, compassion and togetherness that we cherish. We are delighted to be part of an effort that goes beyond celebration to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our children.” This year’s celebration will feature several activities, including free health screenings, face painting, dancing competitions, a bouncy castle, health talks and inspiring sessions with well-known personalities. The children will also enjoy food, drinks and gifts as part of the celebration. Over the years, Philip Nai & Friends has used the Christmas season as an opportunity to give back to society and create memorable experiences for children who may otherwise have limited opportunities to enjoy the festivities. The initiative is calling on individuals, corporate organisations and well-meaning members of the public to support this year’s outreach through donations, volunteering and other forms of assistance. Those interested in supporting the initiative can contact the organisers on 0244 735 451. The seventh edition is supported by Joy FM, Sonotech Medical and Diagnostic Centre, Gigi’s Kitchen, Women of Valour, Remedy Hearts Foundation, The Brands People Limited and TW Radio. Philip Nai & Friends continues to champion a simple but powerful message: Sharing. Giving. Inspiring.

items.title: Burkina/Révolution électronique: lancement officiel de l’opération de l’Identifiant Unique
items.description: Le chef de l'Etat burkinabè, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a lancé, officiellement, l'enregistrement national pour l'Identifiant Unique Électronique dans la dynamique de la révolution numérique du Burkina Faso, au cours d’une cérémonie, ce mercredi 11 novembre 2026, à Ouagadougou. Dans le cadre de sa souveraineté numérique, le Burkina Faso, a franchi, un cap historique, ce mercredi 11 novembre 2026. En effet, le gouvernement, à travers le ministère de la Transition digitale, des Postes et des Communications électroniques, a lancé l’opération d’enregistrement national pour l’Identifiant Unique Electronique (IUE) de la personne physique, lors d’une cérémonie présidée par le président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, ce mercredi 11 novembre 2026. Selon le Département de la Transition digitale, l’IUE va doter le Burkina Faso «d'un fichier national assaini, garantissant l'unicité absolue de chaque personne enregistrée tout en simplifiant radicalement les démarches administratives». «Nous avons pris le soin d'avoir d'abord un système informatique … conçu, développé et sécurisé par des ingénieurs burkinabè, par les techniciens de notre pays. Cela va nous permettre d'économiser énormément, en ce sens que beaucoup de structures ont besoin de prestataires, ont besoin de données biométriques», a déclaré le chef de l’Etat, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Le président du Faso s’est réjoui du lancement de ce système, porté par des intelligences au plan national, qui permettra de mettre fin à la dépendance des prestataires extérieurs et de rationaliser les dépenses publiques. Sur les caractéristiques techniques du système, la ministre de la Transition digitale, des Postes et des Communications électroniques, Aminata Zerbo/Sabané, a indiqué que l'IUE repose sur la capture biométrique complète de l'usager, incluant «l’empreinte numérique des dix doigts; l'image haute définition des deux iris et une photographie faciale normée». Selon Mme Zerbo, l'enregistrement concerne l'ensemble des personnes physiques présentes sur le territoire burkinabè, sans distinction d'âge et prend en compte les nouveau-nés dès la déclaration de leur naissance. Elle a poursuivi que le déploiement national s'effectuera par vagues régionales successives jusqu'en juillet 2027 avec une feuille de route logistique prévoyant la mobilisation de moyens exceptionnels: «plus de 12 000 sites d'enregistrement fixes et mobiles à travers les 13 régions; plus de 900 kits d'enrôlement biométrique de pointe; plus de 2 400 agents de terrain mobilisés avec le concours du Programme National de Volontariat du Burkina Faso (PNVB) et un support logistique assuré par l'opérateur public La Poste BF». Par Wakat Séra L’article Burkina/Révolution électronique: lancement officiel de l’opération de l’Identifiant Unique est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: TOR reduces negative equity from GH¢7.5bn to GH¢5bn – Kombat
items.description: The Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) says it has reduced its negative equity from GH¢7.5 billion to GH¢5 billion as part of efforts to restore its financial stability. Managing Director of TOR, Edmond Kombat, says the improvement forms part of a broader restructuring programme aimed at strengthening the refinery’s balance sheet and positioning it for long-term sustainability. Speaking on the second day of the Ghana Economic Forum organised by the Business & Financial Times (B&FT), he said management is working to move the refinery from negative to positive equity through debt restructuring and a revaluation of its assets. “We had inherited a negative equity of 7.5 billion. At the end of 2025, it came down to 5 billion,” he said. Mr Kombat disclosed that the refinery’s assets were last valued in 2009, prompting management to engage valuers to undertake a fresh assessment. “The last time the refinery was valued was 2009. We’ve brought back the valuers to revalue it,” he stated. He said the objective is to clean up the refinery’s balance sheet, restructure its debt and achieve a positive equity position ahead of a planned listing on the Ghana Stock Exchange in 2028. “We want to clean it and move to a positive equity and restructure the debt and we are targeting 2028 to list it,” he added. Mr Kombat said management is also targeting at least three years of sustained profitability before the proposed listing, which he believes will attract private-sector investment and strengthen the refinery’s corporate governance.

items.title: 2027: S’west monarchs back southern presidency, endorse Tinubu, support state police
items.description: …reject fuel subsidy return, urge peaceful elections, commend new military formations in Oyo, Ekiti By Adeola Badru Traditional rulers from across the South-West have endorsed the continuation of the presidency in Southern Nigeria beyond the 2027 general elections, declaring that sustaining the principle of power rotation is critical to national unity, political stability, equity and inclusiveness. The monarchs also reaffirmed their unwavering support for President Bola Tinubu and his administration while backing the proposed establishment of state police as part of efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s security architecture. These were among the major resolutions reached at a meeting of the South-West Council of Obas and Traditional Rulers held at the Aafin Olubadan, Oke Aremo, Ibadan, Oyo State, on Wednesday. The meeting, which brought together prominent traditional rulers from the six South-West states, also endorsed the Federal Government’s position against the reintroduction of fuel subsidy, called for peaceful and credible elections in 2027, and urged greater collaboration among Nigeria’s geopolitical regions. In a communiqué issued and read by the Alake of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Gbadebo, at the end of the meeting, said the rotational presidency arrangement had contributed significantly to political stability, inclusiveness and national cohesion, stressing that the arrangement should be sustained in the next electoral cycle. The Council declared, “The principle of rotational presidency has, over the years, contributed significantly to political stability, inclusiveness, and national cohesion across Nigeria.” “In the interest of fairness, equity, and the continued strengthening of national unity, the Council expressed the view that the rotational arrangement should be sustained and that the presidency should remain in Southern Nigeria in the next electoral cycle, in line with the spirit of power rotation that has helped preserve peace and stability in the country.” The monarchs explained that their position was informed by the need to strengthen mutual trust among the federating units and preserve the delicate balance required for the country’s continued progress. They added that the position was intended to promote “national balance, mutual trust among the federating units, and the continued progress of the Nigerian State”. On the 2027 general elections, the traditional rulers called on political parties, candidates and the electorate to embrace democratic values and shun activities capable of undermining the electoral process. They condemned electoral violence, intimidation, vote-buying and other forms of electoral malpractice, emphasising the need for peaceful, free and credible elections at all levels. “The Council underscored the importance of peaceful, free, and credible elections at all levels. It condemned all forms of electoral violence, intimidation, vote-buying, and other electoral malpractices, urging political actors and citizens alike to uphold democratic values before, during, and after elections,” the communiqué stated. On national leadership, the monarchs unanimously reaffirmed their support for President Tinubu, acknowledging the efforts of the Federal Government in addressing the country’s challenges and advancing its development agenda. The Council also urged traditional rulers across the region to intensify grassroots mobilisation and sensitisation to encourage citizens to support government programmes and policies aimed at promoting economic growth, national stability and social development. “The Council unanimously reaffirmed its unwavering support for His Excellency, the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, and his administration,” the communiqué stated. It added that the monarchs acknowledged the federal government’s efforts towards addressing national challenges and advancing the country’s development agenda. The Council’s position on the proposed state police initiative was equally emphatic, with the monarchs describing it as a strategic intervention capable of strengthening internal security and improving responses to security threats across the country. They urged traditional rulers to begin preparing and sensitising youths within their respective domains to take advantage of employment and other service opportunities that might emerge from the initiative. “The Council expressed support for the proposed establishment of State Police as a strategic measure to strengthen internal security,” the communiqué said. It further encouraged monarchs across the Southwest to prepare young people in their communities for opportunities that could arise from the proposed security arrangement. On the controversial fuel subsidy policy, the traditional rulers aligned themselves with the Federal Government’s current position, arguing that a return to the subsidy regime would not serve Nigeria’s long-term economic interests. While acknowledging the economic realities confronting the country, the monarchs maintained that fiscal sustainability and national economic development should remain central to policy decisions. “The Council noted the economic realities confronting the nation and expressed support for the Federal Government’s current position on fuel subsidy.” “The meeting resolved that the reintroduction of fuel subsidy would not serve the long-term interests of national economic development and fiscal sustainability,” the communiqué stated. The monarchs also called for stronger political and economic engagement to ensure that the interests of the South-West were adequately represented and protected within the Nigerian federation. They stressed the need for the region to remain vigilant and strategically engaged in national affairs, particularly on issues affecting its political relevance, economic advancement and developmental aspirations. Beyond regional interests, the Council called for stronger national integration and constructive engagement among traditional institutions across the country’s geopolitical zones. It pledged to strengthen relationships with traditional rulers in Northern Nigeria and other parts of the federation, noting that mutual understanding and cooperation remained essential to peace, unity and national development. “Recognising the importance of national integration, the Council called for stronger collaboration and mutual understanding among all regions of the country.” “The traditional rulers pledged to foster constructive engagement with their counterparts in Northern Nigeria and other parts of the federation in the interest of peace, unity, and national development,” the communiqué stated. The meeting also commended President Tinubu for the establishment of a new military brigade in Oyo State, describing the development as a significant boost to the security architecture of the South-West. The monarchs expressed appreciation to the president for the military formation, noting that it would strengthen security operations and contribute to the protection of lives and property across the region. “The Council expressed profound appreciation to the President for the establishment of the new military brigade in Oyo State,” the communiqué stated. The traditional rulers added that the development would significantly enhance the region’s security architecture and contribute to safeguarding communities against security threats. They also commended the President and the Federal Government for ongoing infrastructure projects and other developmental initiatives across the South-West and the country. According to the Council, the projects had continued to contribute positively to economic activities, improved connectivity and overall national development. “The meeting acknowledged the positive impact of these projects on economic activities, connectivity, and overall national development,” the communiqué added. The monarchs further resolved to maintain regular consultations and strategic engagements on issues affecting the welfare, security and development of the South-West and Nigeria as a whole. In their concluding remarks, the monarchs reaffirmed their commitment to peace, good governance, national unity and sustainable development, urging Nigerians to remain law-abiding, support legitimate government initiatives and work collectively towards building a more prosperous and secure country. The meeting, which was hosted by the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, attracted the Ooni of Ife, Oba Enitan Ogunwusi; the Alake of Egbaland; the Ewi of Ado-Ekiti; the Soun of Ogbomosho; the Deji of Akure; and the Elegushi of Ikate-Elegushi, among other prominent traditional rulers. Other monarchs listed as participants included the Ogoga of Ikere-Ekiti, Ajero of Ijero, Ayangburen of Ikorodu, Alara of Ilara Epe, Oniru of Iru-land, Oniba of Iba, Osolu of Irewe, Olu of Ilaro, Akarigbo of Remo-land, Olofin of Isheri, Ebunmawe of Ago-Iwoye, Olowo of Owo, Owa Obokun of Ijeshaland and Orangun of Oke-Ila. The meeting brought together traditional rulers from Ekiti, Lagos, Ogun, Ondo, Osun and Oyo states, underscoring the Council’s regional character and its determination to strengthen the traditional institution’s involvement in matters of national importance. items.title: 2027: APC resorts to cash, gifts to mask Tinubu’s failures – ADC
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of using cash, food and gifts at political gatherings to mask the failures of President Bola Tinubu’s administration and manufacture public support ahead of the 2027 elections. The council said the reported handouts were an attempt to buy political enthusiasm at a time millions of Nigerians were struggling with the cost of food, transportation and other basic necessities, insisting that temporary inducements could not erase the hardship confronting households. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the ADC PCC cited reports of luxury vehicles allegedly presented to APC women leaders, cash and cooked food distributed by the President’s son through the City Boy Movement, as well as videos showing an APC women leader sharing money and fabrics. “The pattern is becoming impossible to ignore,” the council said, citing the reported distributions as evidence of what it described as the ruling party’s attempt to turn political support into a commodity. “From reports of luxury vehicles presented to APC women leaders, to cash and cooked food distributed by the President’s son through the City Boy Movement, and now videos circulating of an APC women leader handing out money and fabrics, the ruling party appears to be treating political support as something that can be bought,” it added. The ADC PCC described the reported distributions as particularly insensitive given the economic difficulties facing ordinary Nigerians. “After three and a half years of economic hardship, rising insecurity and mounting public debt, the APC has little to show Nigerians. Its answer is to display cash and gifts at political events, as though a brief handout can erase the daily struggle families face or buy their votes,” the council said. It also questioned what it described as selective enforcement of currency laws, demanding that the authorities explain why ordinary Nigerians were pursued over alleged abuse of the naira while reported cash distributions at political gatherings appeared to attract a different response. “The same authorities that have pursued ordinary Nigerians over alleged abuse of the Naira must explain why apparent cash distribution by political operatives at campaign events should be treated differently. The EFCC and INEC must investigate these incidents and take appropriate action wherever electoral or currency laws have been breached,” it said. On the administration’s borrowing, the council demanded greater accountability over the scale, terms and utilisation of government loans, arguing that the financial burden on Nigerians remained a major concern. “The Tinubu administration has pushed millions deeper into poverty, while Nigerians continue to demand answers about the scale, terms and use of government borrowing. Cash, gifts and staged displays cannot conceal a record of failure,” the ADC PCC added. It insisted that neither financial inducements nor elaborate political gatherings could dictate how Nigerians would vote in 2027. “No amount of money can compel Nigerians to endorse a government that has made life harder for them. The people’s votes are not for sale, and no manufactured crowd can substitute for their verdict at the ballot box,” the council declared. The ADC PCC urged the EFCC and INEC to investigate the reported distributions and publicly disclose the steps being taken, warning that political parties must not be allowed to use cash or gifts to compromise electoral integrity. It maintained that the ultimate test of the APC’s popularity would not be the size of crowds or the volume of gifts distributed at political gatherings, but the verdict Nigerians deliver at the ballot box. WEAR Ghana, Republic of Africa win CANEX Creative Pitch 2026 in Lagos
items.description: Ghanaian creative entrepreneur Awura Abena Agyeman has won the CANEX Creative Pitch 2026 in Lagos, Nigeria, with a presentation on the evolution of WEAR Ghana into the pan-African cultural enterprise, Republic of Africa. The competition formed part of Creative Africa Nexus Weekend (CANEX WKND), organised by the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank). The gathering brings together entrepreneurs, artists, investors, policymakers and other stakeholders to explore opportunities for financing, collaboration and growth across Africa’s creative industries. Awura Abena Agyeman’s presentation traced the evolution of WEAR Ghana, established in 2013 to encourage greater appreciation for locally produced clothing, into a business that has combined contemporary fashion with African cultural identity. Among its notable successes is GIGI, a collection incorporating African wax-print details, which became a signature product following its introduction in 2016 and continues to sell around the world, 10 years later. The presentation also introduced the broader vision behind Republic of Africa, launched in May 2025 as a pan-African cultural initiative seeking to connect people across borders through fashion, creativity and shared identity. Beyond the business journey, Awura Abena Agyeman highlighted the importance of employment, skills development and local production in creating opportunities within Africa’s creative economy. Her recognition at CANEX comes amid growing conversations about the economic potential of African creativity and the need for stronger local participation in the industries built around the continent’s cultural influence. The achievement also underscores the role of platforms such as CANEX in creating opportunities for African creative entrepreneurs to engage directly with potential investors and industry leaders. For WEAR Ghana and Republic of Africa, the victory represents another chapter in a journey that began with a simple ambition to encourage Ghanaians to wear Ghanaian-made clothing and has since grown into a wider vision of African cultural connection and enterprise.
